events.body: The Hawk houses of Siorrachd Cnoc bheag name a custodian of their own, Raonaid nic Iain, and seat her at Inis ìseal. The high custodian at Seann Skell will not own her. The houses carry on as if he had.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Òrd an t-Seabhaig gather at Inis ìseal to name a custodian

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh Ruadh gives Raonaid the kept feather

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seann Skell's letter refusing Raonaid reaches Inis ìseal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Òrd an t-Seabhaig carry on as if the custodian had been owned

events.title: Òrd an t-Seabhaig gather at Inis ìseal to name a custodian
events.body: Witnesses of every Hawk house in Siorrachd Cnoc bheag crowd the hall at Inis ìseal and name Raonaid nic Iain custodian by a standing vote, each house setting meal, wool or honey on the altar's step before the hall breaks.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Hawk houses' own custodian

told_in.section: I. Of the Naming at Inis ìseal

events.title: Murchadh Ruadh gives Raonaid the kept feather
events.body: Murchadh Ruadh of Baile fhraoich sets a white feather kept three generations in his own house into Raonaid nic Iain's hand at her naming, and she wears it pinned at her collar from that day.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Hawk houses' own custodian

told_in.section: I. Of the Naming at Inis ìseal

events.title: Òrd an t-Seabhaig speak of a hawk for the shire's arms
events.body: Witnesses leaving Raonaid nic Iain's naming say openly that Siorrachd Cnoc bheag's white billet, the roll's mark for two ages, ought to be struck for a hawk, though no house yet carries the saying south.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A hawk for Siorrachd Cnoc bheag

told_in.section: I. Of the Naming at Inis ìseal

events.title: Seann Skell's letter refusing Raonaid reaches Inis ìseal
events.body: A three-line letter from Àrd-choimheadaiche's house at Seann Skell in the south reaches Inis ìseal, naming no fault in Raonaid nic Iain but saying Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail's own order of worship knows no office of a Hawk custodian and so cannot own her.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Hawk houses' own custodian

told_in.section: II. Of the Letter from Seann Skell in the South

events.title: Òrd an t-Seabhaig carry on as if the custodian had been owned
events.body: Òrd an t-Seabhaig fold the southern letter away unanswered and keep bringing their vigils and disputes to Raonaid nic Iain exactly as before, burying and marrying their own under no rite but hers.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Hawk houses' own custodian

told_in.section: II. Of the Letter from Seann Skell in the South

events.title: Raonaid nic Iain at Inis ìseal
events.body: Raonaid nic Iain, custodian of the Hawk houses, writes out the Hawk's order of worship, which until now was spoken and never written. The Hawk houses read it aloud once a year and keep the written copy locked away.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raonaid begins setting Òrd an t-Seabhaig's order into a farm account-book

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The order finished and locked in the altar's oil-box

events.title: Raonaid begins setting Òrd an t-Seabhaig's order into a farm account-book
events.body: Raonaid nic Iain starts writing Òrd an t-Seabhaig's spoken order of worship, till then carried only in a custodian's memory, into a farmer's account-book, sounding each line against the altar to match her own mother's mother's telling of it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raonaid nic Iain at Inis ìseal

told_in.section: III. Of the Order Set Down

events.title: The order finished and locked in the altar's oil-box
events.body: Raonaid nic Iain finishes the written order at the turn of the year, reads it aloud once to the gathered houses, ties it with a strip of white feather and locks it into the iron box that once held the altar's lamp-oil.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raonaid nic Iain at Inis ìseal

told_in.section: III. Of the Order Set Down

events.title: A hawk for Siorrachd Cnoc bheag
events.body: The Hawk houses of Siorrachd Cnoc bheag ask the council to set a hawk on the shire's arms in place of the white billet the roll gave it. The council grants it, and the maor's seal is recut with a white hawk among its twelve crescents. It is the first change made to the roll at the asking of an order.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Òrd an t-Seabhaig speak of a hawk for the shire's arms

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A delegation from Inis ìseal asks the council for a hawk on the shire's seal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The maor breaks the old die and presses the new seal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raonaid holds the new seal

events.title: A delegation from Inis ìseal asks the council for a hawk on the shire's seal
events.body: Five witnesses from Òrd an t-Seabhaig, Raonaid nic Iain among them, ride to Cathair dhearg to ask the council that Siorrachd Cnoc bheag's white billet be struck and a hawk set on the shire's arms in its place.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A hawk for Siorrachd Cnoc bheag

told_in.section: IV. Of the Hawk on the Seal

events.title: The maor breaks the old die and presses the new seal
events.body: The maor of Siorrachd Cnoc bheag breaks the shire's old die before its assembled clerks and presses the recut seal, a white hawk among twelve crescents, into wax for the first time.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A hawk for Siorrachd Cnoc bheag

told_in.section: IV. Of the Hawk on the Seal

events.title: Six dead at the Còmhrag
events.body: Six fighters die at the Còmhrag, the most in any year yet. The custodians of the Rite petition for its ending. The fair-wardens of Ceann leathan, whose town lives off the crowds, refuse.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Six die at that year's Còmhrag

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The custodians' petition against Còmhrag Ceann leathan is refused

events.title: Six die at that year's Còmhrag
events.body: Six fighters, the most in any year yet, die on the trampled ground at Ceann leathan before that year's Còmhrag is called, one of them a boy of Baile ghlas not yet twenty.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Six dead at the Còmhrag

told_in.section: V. Of What the North Carried That Year Besides

events.title: The custodians' petition against Còmhrag Ceann leathan is refused
events.body: The custodians of the southern Rite petition the fair-wardens of Ceann leathan in writing to end Còmhrag Ceann leathan after six deaths; the wardens read it and refuse within the hour, on the ground the town lives off Còmhrag Ceann leathan's crowds.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Six dead at the Còmhrag

told_in.section: V. Of What the North Carried That Year Besides

events.title: The circus at Ceann leathan
events.body: In the year of the six dead An Siorcas Siubhail Do-thuigsinn pitches at Ceann leathan and plays to the crowds who stay on after the melee. It is said the fair-wardens paid it to come.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: An Siorcas Siubhail Do-thuigsinn pitches at Ceann leathan after the six burials

events.title: An Siorcas Siubhail Do-thuigsinn pitches at Ceann leathan after the six burials
events.body: An Siorcas Siubhail Do-thuigsinn pitches its tents on Còmhrag Ceann leathan's own trampled ground within a week of the six burials, and it is said, though never proved, that the fair-wardens paid it to come.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The circus at Ceann leathan

told_in.section: V. Of What the North Carried That Year Besides

events.title: The coal line reaches Ceann leathan
events.body: The railway is carried through to the port of Ceann leathan, so that coal may be shipped from a second harbour. The quays of Ceann leathan are rebuilt for coal-ships, and the town outgrows its walls.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first coal-ship loads by lamplight at Ceann leathan

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ceann leathan's quays outrun its walls

events.title: The first coal-ship loads by lamplight at Ceann leathan
events.body: The first coal-ship out of Ceann leathan's rebuilt quays loads by lamplight on a winter tide, the harbour clerk noting only the hour, the tonnage and the shore gang's complaint of the cold.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The coal line reaches Ceann leathan

told_in.section: V. Of What the North Carried That Year Besides

events.title: Ros bheag's shipyard
events.body: Ros bheag on the west coast opens a yard for coal-ships, and the western ports need no longer send to Ros dhomhain for hulls. The shipwrights of Ros dhomhain protest to the guild court and lose.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ros dhomhain's masters lose their protest at the guild court

events.title: Ros dhomhain's masters lose their protest at the guild court
events.body: The eldest masters of Ros dhomhain carry their protest against Ros bheag's new coal-ship yard to the guild court at Cathair dhearg and lose it in a single sitting, the court ruling a guild's charter binds no yard to a monopoly of the coast.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ros bheag's shipyard

told_in.section: V. Of What the North Carried That Year Besides

events.title: Ceann leathan's quays outrun its walls
events.body: Within two winters of Slighe a' Ghuail's coming the quays of Ceann leathan spread half a mile beyond the old gate with no wall following them, so that a stranger riding in from the coast road can no longer say where the town begins.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The coal line reaches Ceann leathan

told_in.section: V. Of What the North Carried That Year Besides

events.title: Raonaid holds the new seal
events.body: Raonaid nic Iain holds the recut seal of Siorrachd Cnoc bheag in her own hands the day it reaches Inis ìseal, the hawk's wing cut spread rather than folded, and says nothing for a while that any witness troubles to write down.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A hawk for Siorrachd Cnoc bheag

told_in.section: IV. Of the Hawk on the Seal

events.title: Iain Mapa proves the deep gallery
events.body: Sent to measure a new shaft cut on a guild captain's thirty-year hunch, Iain mac Ruairidh finds the silver at Muileann chiar running richer with depth rather than thinner, the ore darker and heavier the further the gallery goes. He checks the figures three times before he writes them fair.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The silver at depth

told_in.section: I. Of the Faces below the Old Working

events.title: The silver at depth
events.body: The silver seam at Muileann chiar, which the Dia-thìrich kept in their own hands through the humans' time, is found richer at depth than any had looked for. The town's old silver guild takes a charter under the restored custom. Iain Mapa, working there since the Board sent him, measures the new faces.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Mapa proves the deep gallery

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The guild masters read the survey entire

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Comann an Airgid of Muileann chiar chartered anew

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Mapa marries Mòr nic Dhòmhnaill

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Mapa keeps a second copy of the guild's charter

events.title: The eastern blank-houses
events.body: More silver comes up from Muileann chiar than the mint at Cathair dhearg can refine. The Crown gives the villages of the eastern hills the refining of the guild's bar, with the gold washed from the stream below Baile dhìreach, into blanks for the realm-coin. The mint strikes them. The villages are paid by weight.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gold found in the stream below Baile dhìreach

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first blanks struck for the mint

events.title: Dùn thais in the west
events.body: Dùn thais on the west coast is granted a court of the sea of its own, to judge salvage and wreck along its shore. At its first sitting it awards a raider's hulk to the fishermen who drove it aground.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dùn thais in the west granted a sea court

events.title: The guild masters read the survey entire
events.body: Iain carries the deep gallery's figures to the guild hall himself and unrolls them before three masters who argue over the timbering a new shaft will need. He tells them plainly it will hold only if timbered as he has drawn it, and not an inch cheaper.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The silver at depth

told_in.section: I. Of the Faces below the Old Working

events.title: Comann an Airgid of Muileann chiar chartered anew
events.body: On the strength of the deep gallery's yield the council renews under the restored custom the charter the humans' own Administration had let stand and then let lapse, binding the guild's captains to An Crùn's tithe on every bar struck and giving the guild the courts' weight behind its bindings.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The silver at depth

told_in.section: I. Of the Faces below the Old Working

events.title: Gold found in the stream below Baile dhìreach
events.body: A village smith washing his pan of an evening finds fine gold in the gravel of the stream that turns his forge's own wheel, and tells a maor's clerk the plain truth when the coin he has put by draws the clerk's question rather than invent a lie he would have to keep.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The eastern blank-houses

told_in.section: II. Of the Blanks and the Gold below Baile dhìreach

events.title: The first blanks struck for the mint
events.body: More silver comes up from Muileann chiar than the mint at Cathair dhearg can refine, and the council gives the eastern hill villages the refining of the guild's bar, with the gold washed below Baile dhìreach, into blanks for Bonn na Rìoghachd, paid by weight; the first blanks go north in am Faoilleach.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The eastern blank-houses

told_in.section: II. Of the Blanks and the Gold below Baile dhìreach

events.title: Dùn thais in the east
events.body: The other Dùn thais, in the east, seat of its own shire, builds a covered market for the hill farms. For ten years the royal record confuses the courts of the two towns, until Tormod Pinn marks them west and east.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dùn thais in the east opens its covered market

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The royal record confuses the two Dùn thais

events.title: Siorrachd Doire chaol
events.body: Doire chaol, the village laid out south of the capital for the families of the royal household, has grown too great for the maor of Baile chiar to govern from his seat. The council cuts it out as a shire of its own, the only shire made since the drawing.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile chiar's maor petitions to cut out Doire chaol

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Siorrachd Doire chaol cut from Baile chiar

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Baile chiar maor glad of the lightening

events.title: Iain Mapa marries Mòr nic Dhòmhnaill
events.body: Iain marries Mòr, a refiner's daughter of Muileann chiar who first proved his own scale a hair off true in front of three of the guild's captains. They are married at the guild hall in am Faoilleach, her father giving her hand and the guild's captains standing witness in place of Iain's own western kin.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The silver at depth

told_in.section: III. Of Mòr nic Dhòmhnaill

events.title: Dùn thais in the west granted a sea court
events.body: The western Dùn thais is granted a court of the sea to judge salvage and wreck along its shore, after a wrecked hulk driven ashore proves too rich a prize for custom alone to divide. The court's first sitting, held on the strand, awards the wreck whole to the crews who drove it aground.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dùn thais in the west

told_in.section: IV. Of the Two Towns Called Dùn thais

events.title: Dùn thais in the east opens its covered market
events.body: The eastern Dùn thais raises a covered market at its own shire's charge for the hill farms that had traded in its square uncovered since the town was walled, its first trading held under a roof that smells more of new-cut wood than of the produce it shelters.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dùn thais in the east

told_in.section: IV. Of the Two Towns Called Dùn thais

events.title: The royal record confuses the two Dùn thais
events.body: A clerk at Cathair dhearg files the western court's petition and the eastern market's petition against the one town's name, both signed only "Dùn thais", and a second clerk's hand-correction holds only until the next season's post brings the same confusion again.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dùn thais in the east

told_in.section: IV. Of the Two Towns Called Dùn thais

events.title: Baile chiar's maor petitions to cut out Doire chaol
events.body: The maor of Baile chiar writes plainly that Doire chaol, grown from a scattering of household-clerks' houses into a town proper, has outgrown a seat five miles distant, and asks that it be given a maor of its own rather than go on being governed badly at second hand.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Siorrachd Doire chaol

told_in.section: V. Of the Petition from Baile chiar

events.title: Siorrachd Doire chaol cut from Baile chiar
events.body: The council grants the petition before the summer is old, the only shire cut new from an older one since the original drawing, Doire chaol entered onto the roll with its own arms, its own dues, and a maor of its own choosing.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Siorrachd Doire chaol

told_in.section: V. Of the Petition from Baile chiar

events.title: The Baile chiar maor glad of the lightening
events.body: The maor of Baile chiar, reading the grant that cuts Siorrachd Doire chaol from his shire, tells his clerk he is glad of the lightening, and sends the new shire's first dues south the same season with a note wishing its maor better luck of it than he had had.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Siorrachd Doire chaol

told_in.section: V. Of the Petition from Baile chiar

events.title: The dead and not dead of Doire uaine
events.body: Herders near Doire uaine will not graze the hills above the town, where old writings tell of a thing that is dead and does not rest. A shepherd is lost there. The magistrate enters wolves.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A shepherd lost above Doire uaine

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The magistrate enters wolves at Doire uaine

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Mapa keeps a second copy of the guild's charter

events.title: The fall at Muileann dhearg
events.body: A gallery of the reopened Cill ghlas district gives way under Muileann dhearg, along a line the surveyors had marked as sound. Thirty-one hewers die. It is small beside the Rending. It is the same fault.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Mapa rides through the night to Muileann dhearg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Mapa lays his own old maps against the new fault

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The thirty-one are buried in a single ground

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Mapa writes a letter naming the fault, and does not send it

events.title: Iain Mapa rides through the night to Muileann dhearg
events.body: Word of the fall reaches Muileann chiar by a rider sent without urgency, and Iain Mapa, two seasons into the silver works and no longer reckoned a mine matter by Comhairle nam Mèinnean, rides the thirty miles through the night rather than wait for morning, and goes down on the second rope with a lamp and a level.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fall at Muileann dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Fall at Muileann dhearg
told_in.section: I. Of the First Day of an t-Iuchar

events.title: Iain Mapa lays his own old maps against the new fault
events.body: With maps sent up from Comann an Airgid's own store, older and truer than anything Comhairle nam Mèinnean keeps at Cathair mhòr, Iain Mapa finds the broken ground under the fallen gallery runs exactly where Scàineadh Cill ghlas's own line ran three ages before, marked by an older hand with a single word: left, let be.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fall at Muileann dhearg

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The rules of the shafts

told_in.book: Of the Fall at Muileann dhearg
told_in.section: II. Of the Rules Made for the Dia-thìrich

events.title: The thirty-one are buried in a single ground
events.body: The dead of the fall are buried at the edge of Muileann dhearg's own burying-yard, thirty-one graves broken in two days by every man in the town not needed underground, the district's custodian reading over each grave in turn at the families' own asking, and Iain Mapa standing the whole of it with his hat in his hand.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fall at Muileann dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Fall at Muileann dhearg
told_in.section: II. Of the Rules Made for the Dia-thìrich

events.title: Iain Mapa writes a letter naming the fault, and does not send it
events.body: At his own table at Muileann chiar, Iain Mapa writes to Comhairle nam Mèinnean naming the fault at Cill ghlas by its true line and setting it beside the survey Comhairle nam Mèinnean filed and never circulated three years before; he reads it through twice, folds it, and puts it unsealed in the drawer that holds his old receipt.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fall at Muileann dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Fall at Muileann dhearg
told_in.section: II. Of the Rules Made for the Dia-thìrich

events.title: The rules of the shafts
events.body: After this lesser echo of the old fall of Scàineadh Cill ghlas, new rules for digging are made. They are for Dia-thìrich workers. In the workings where Tuathaich labour they are kept loosely, and by intent.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Mapa lays his own old maps against the new fault

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The new digging rules sent first to Iain Mapa

events.title: The timber at Àth leathan
events.body: At the pits about Àth leathan, where Dia-thìrich overseers work Tuathaich hands, the new rules of timbering are posted and not paid for. The overseers' books, which came later to the library, show the timber ordered and never delivered.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mary Coyle writes to Comhairle nam Mèinnean naming Àth leathan's undelivered timber

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Comhairle nam Mèinnean answers Tional nan Tuathach in three lines and files the matter

events.title: A shepherd lost above Doire uaine
events.body: A shepherd new to the country puts his flock to the one shoulder of hill the town's shepherds will not graze, where the old writings tell of the Marbh-bheò, and does not come down. His dog returns alone; the town finds only his crook, driven upright into the turf.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The dead and not dead of Doire uaine

told_in.section: VI. Of the Shepherd above Doire uaine

events.title: The magistrate enters wolves at Doire uaine
events.body: The magistrate writes wolves as the cause in the shire's own book, a finding no shepherd argues and none believes, since no wolf has been seen on that hill in living memory. He tells the shepherd's mother the book wanted a cause it could hold.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The dead and not dead of Doire uaine

told_in.section: VI. Of the Shepherd above Doire uaine

events.title: Iain Mapa keeps a second copy of the guild's charter
events.body: Iain writes Comann an Airgid's new charter into his own private book beside the receipt he carried from An Sloc Mòr and the deep gallery's own figures, telling Mòr at last that Comhairle nam Mèinnean never once told him his first survey of the thinning vein had proved true.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The silver at depth

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The dead and not dead of Doire uaine

told_in.section: VII. Of the Copy Iain Kept

events.title: Mary Coyle writes to Comhairle nam Mèinnean naming Àth leathan's undelivered timber
events.body: Reading a copy of Comhairle nam Mèinnean's new digging rules brought north by a carter, Mary Coyle writes in Tional nan Tuathach's own hand asking that the rules be kept in fact at the western pits as well as in the posting, and names Àth leathan and the ordered timber that never left the yard at Ceann mhòr.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The timber at Àth leathan

told_in.book: Of the Fall at Muileann dhearg
told_in.section: III. Of the Sixty and the Forty

events.title: Comhairle nam Mèinnean answers Tional nan Tuathach in three lines and files the matter
events.body: Comhairle nam Mèinnean thanks Tional nan Tuathach for its concern and states that Àth leathan's timber has been referred to the district overseer for his report; no report is ever filed, and Mary Coyle's letter is kept, unanswered further, in the press at Cathair mhòr where papers go that Comhairle nam Mèinnean has no further use for.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The timber at Àth leathan

told_in.book: Of the Fall at Muileann dhearg
told_in.section: III. Of the Sixty and the Forty

events.title: The new digging rules sent first to Iain Mapa
events.body: Comhairle nam Mèinnean's new rules for digging after the fall are sent first to Iain Mapa at Muileann dhearg as the man who closed the district, and he finds nothing in them he would change; they are made for Dia-thìrich workers.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The rules of the shafts

told_in.book: Of the Fall at Muileann dhearg
told_in.section: II. Of the Rules Made for the Dia-thìrich

events.title: Ailean Leabhar is found dead at his own desk
events.body: On the third day of an t-Sultain, Mòrag nic Coinnich finds Ailean Leabhar at his desk at Muileann chaol, the harvest returns for Siorrachd Doire chaol open under his hand and his pen laid down beside them rather than dropped, so that he seems, she says after, to have finished the line he was writing before he stopped.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Mòrag nic Coinnich, keeper

told_in.book: Of the Fall at Muileann dhearg
told_in.section: IV. Of the Third Day of an t-Sultain

events.title: Mòrag nic Coinnich, keeper
events.body: Ailean Leabhar dies at Muileann chaol, and Mòrag nic Coinnich becomes keeper of the library. She begins the custom, kept ever since, of writing beside each item whence it came.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailean Leabhar is found dead at his own desk

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailean Leabhar is buried in the ground behind an Leabharlann

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mòrag nic Coinnich finds an unfinished note among Ailean Leabhar's papers

events.title: Ailean Leabhar is buried in the ground behind an Leabharlann
events.body: Ailean Leabhar is buried two days after at Muileann chaol, in a small ground behind an Leabharlann itself where no keeper had been buried before him, the town turning out near to the last household, and Mòrag nic Coinnich reads over him only his own words, that an Leabharlann settles nothing and only keeps.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Mòrag nic Coinnich, keeper

told_in.book: Of the Fall at Muileann dhearg
told_in.section: IV. Of the Third Day of an t-Sultain

events.title: Mòrag nic Coinnich finds an unfinished note among Ailean Leabhar's papers
events.body: Going through the old keeper's desk in her first month as keeper, Mòrag nic Coinnich finds one sheet in his own hand, undated beyond an old year, reading only that what an Leabharlann is not sent it cannot keep, and to ask the shires again; she cannot say whether it was a note to himself or the start of a letter, and keeps it unfiled in her own drawer.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Mòrag nic Coinnich, keeper

told_in.book: Of the Fall at Muileann dhearg
told_in.section: IV. Of the Third Day of an t-Sultain

events.title: The pit families of Achadh dhomhain
events.body: After the fall at Muileann dhearg forty hewers' families leave Achadh dhomhain for the fishing ports of the south. The Guild of Hewers binds sixty apprentices to fill its rolls. None of them are Tuathaich.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Sixty apprentices are bound at Achadh dhomhain, and not one is Tuathaich

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A family with no dead in the fall leaves Achadh dhomhain regardless

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Forty households entered 'gone south'

events.title: Sixty apprentices are bound at Achadh dhomhain, and not one is Tuathaich
events.body: Comann nan Gualadairean binds sixty boys in its own hall at Achadh dhomhain to fill the rolls the fall thinned by thirty-one, each swearing with a hand laid on a lump of coal while his father stands behind him in a line the length of the hall, and the charter that reserves the oath to Dia-thìreach applicants is kept to the letter.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pit families of Achadh dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Fall at Muileann dhearg
told_in.section: III. Of the Sixty and the Forty

events.title: A family with no dead in the fall leaves Achadh dhomhain regardless
events.body: Among the forty households that quit Achadh dhomhain for the southern ports that autumn are families who buried no one in the fall, saying to whoever asks that a town may grieve its thirty-one and go on living beside their graves, but a household does not choose to raise its own sons under ground a survey has already misjudged once.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pit families of Achadh dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Fall at Muileann dhearg
told_in.section: III. Of the Sixty and the Forty

events.title: Fire at the fair
events.body: On the eve of Samhain fire runs through the stalls of the fair at Muileann òg. The next day the fair's court sits in a field, and the fair goes on. Oighrig nic Mhathain, toll-mistress since the first fair, dies of her burns.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Oighrig nic Mhathain is burned beating back the fire with her own cloak

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Oighrig nic Mhathain dies of her burns

events.title: Oighrig nic Mhathain is burned beating back the fire with her own cloak
events.body: Caught in the fairground when the fire runs on Samhain eve, Oighrig nic Mhathain beats at the burning canvas with her own cloak until the worst of it is turned from the stalls that hold a dozen towns' whole trade, and does not leave the ground until the last flame along the weavers' row has burned itself out.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Fire at the fair

told_in.book: Of the Fall at Muileann dhearg
told_in.section: V. Of the Fire at the Fair

events.title: The Tuathaich wool carts
events.body: The Rail Board will not carry goods sent by the Moot, pleading the fair's rule on factors. The wool of the north goes south to Muileann òg by cart, five days on the road, and is sold by factors when it comes.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mary Coyle asks Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn whether its reading of the factor rule is new

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The new toll-mistress sells the north's wool through the factors

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Daniel Frayne rides the wool carts south

events.title: Mary Coyle asks Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn whether its reading of the factor rule is new
events.body: When Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn refuses to carry the north's wool on the strength of the fair's own rule on factors, Mary Coyle writes a second, shorter letter asking only whether the reading is new or has simply never before been turned against the north's own goods; Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn does not answer it, and a clerk files it beside the first.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Tuathaich wool carts

told_in.book: Of the Fall at Muileann dhearg
told_in.section: V. Of the Fire at the Fair

events.title: Forty households entered 'gone south'
events.body: The tally-clerk of Achadh dhomhain enters the forty households leaving for the southern ports off the town's roll with two words against each, gone south, the roll keeping no other word for it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pit families of Achadh dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Fall at Muileann dhearg
told_in.section: III. Of the Sixty and the Forty

events.title: Oighrig nic Mhathain dies of her burns
events.body: Oighrig nic Mhathain presides over Cùirt na Fèille from a chair carried into the burnt field, her hands bound in linen, keeps the fair open to its appointed end, and dies of her burns at her own house at Muileann òg before the month is out, fifty years old.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Fire at the fair

told_in.book: Of the Fall at Muileann dhearg
told_in.section: V. Of the Fire at the Fair

events.title: The new toll-mistress sells the north's wool through the factors
events.body: The new toll-mistress at Muileann òg, keeping the fair's rules as Oighrig left them, sells the north's cart-borne wool through the factors when it comes, and enters the sale in the fair's book under the makers' shire.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Tuathaich wool carts

told_in.book: Of the Fall at Muileann dhearg
told_in.section: V. Of the Fire at the Fair

events.title: The Tuathaich carters' road
events.body: The carters of the northern wool go to the fair by Cnoc ghorm, Àth fhada and the old road down to Inis àrsaidh, and the Tuathaich villages on the way open inns for them. In the north the road is called the Carters' Road. In the south it has no name.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Daniel Frayne rides the wool carts south

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first lamp lit at Àth fhada

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The north's name and the south's silence

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A season's wages weighed against the road

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wool train waits out the flood

events.title: Daniel Frayne rides the wool carts south
events.body: With Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn still refusing Tional nan Tuathach's goods, the north's wool goes south by cart, and Daniel Frayne asks leave to ride with the second train, five days on the old way by Cnoc ghorm, Àth fhada and Inis àrsaidh to Fèill Muileann òg.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Tuathaich wool carts

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Tuathaich carters' road

told_in.section: I. Of the Road the North Named

events.title: Dubhan's childhood
events.body: Dubhan grows up watching a caste that does not age hold every true advantage on an island where his own forebears were pushed to the edge. The coal was never his to inherit.

events.title: The Moot's pit register
events.body: The Moot at Caol mhòr begins a register of Tuathaich hewers killed or maimed in the western pits, for no Dia-thìreach book counts them. Mary Coyle's clerks enter the first year's names on the families' own word. The register is kept to this day and has never been sent south.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mary Coyle opens Clàr nan Leòn

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first name entered in Clàr nan Leòn

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A second copy of the register kept apart

events.title: The first lamp lit at Àth fhada
events.body: A widow of Àth fhada who has fed carters at her own table for two winters begins taking payment for it, keeping a lamp lit past every other house's hour. Two more households on the road do the same within the season, and carters find their beds by the lights alone.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Tuathaich carters' road

told_in.section: I. Of the Road the North Named

events.title: The north's name and the south's silence
events.body: Frayne asks the widow at Àth fhada what the carters call their road and learns it has long been called Rathad nan Cairtearan in the north, its name simply grown to fit the wool's going by cart. He learns too that no map south of Cnoc ghorm troubles to name the road at all, and writes both facts down.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Tuathaich carters' road

told_in.section: I. Of the Road the North Named

events.title: A season's wages weighed against the road
events.body: Waiting out a flood at a crossing short of Inis àrsaidh, Frayne hears from a shunting family how the road's five days are reckoned against a season's whole earning, a toll no southern ledger is ever asked to set against the fair's own profit. He writes the figure down.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Tuathaich carters' road

told_in.section: I. Of the Road the North Named

events.title: Mary Coyle opens Clàr nan Leòn
events.body: Mary Coyle tells Tional nan Tuathach's clerks that Comhairle nam Mèinnean keeps no true count of the Tuathaich dead and maimed of the western pits, and that Tional nan Tuathach will begin a book naming them on the families' own word, since no other word will be offered.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Moot's pit register

told_in.section: III. Of the Register Begun

events.title: The first name entered in Clàr nan Leòn
events.body: The widow of Àth fhada's husband, lost under the western pits, is the first name Daniel Frayne writes into the new register, carried south by a neighbour rather than wait on the widow's own journey. Frayne sets the pen down before the ink is dry.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Moot's pit register

told_in.section: III. Of the Register Begun

events.title: The keel laid at Ros mhòr
events.body: Shipwrights turned out of the southern guild yards gather enough coin and timber at last to lay a keel of their own at Ros mhòr. Harry Marlow, grey now, cuts it to the humans' old lines, low and full in the bow, that the southern guilds no longer let a Tuathaich hand build.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ros mhòr's boatyard

told_in.section: V. Of the Keel at Ros mhòr

events.title: The wool train waits out the flood
events.body: The second wool train of the winter sits a night at the flooded crossing short of Inis àrsaidh and goes on when the water drops, losing half a day to the weather and none of the wool, its lead carter holding that a road worn long enough finds its own way round a flood.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Tuathaich carters' road

told_in.section: I. Of the Road the North Named

events.title: Ros mhòr's boatyard
events.body: Tuathaich boatbuilders turned out of the guild yards open a boatyard at Ros mhòr in the north. Its boats are built to the humans' old lines and are swifter than anything in the south.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The keel laid at Ros mhòr

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first Ros mhòr hull launched

events.title: Tormod Pinn
events.body: Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill lays down the office of royal chronicler. Tormod mac Sheumais follows her, called Tormod Pinn for the speed of his hand. He keeps the record for more than twenty years and writes more of it than any before or since.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill's last entry

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Pinn copies the list of gaps

events.title: A second copy of the register kept apart
events.body: By the year's end the register holds above thirty names. A second copy is made against fire or flood and kept at a house in Muileann leathan, so that no single hand's slipping can lose the names a second time.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Moot's pit register

told_in.section: III. Of the Register Begun

events.title: Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill's last entry
events.body: Feeling her hand begin to shake on a long day's writing, Gormshuil lays down the office of royal chronicler after four and twenty years, her final entry a plain list of what Eachdraidh na Rìoghachd under her hand had never held: the northern towns' own accounts, the humans' old treaties, and Comhairle nam Mèinnean's surveys left unrolled.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tormod Pinn

told_in.section: IV. Of the Chronicle Laid Down

events.title: Tormod Pinn copies the list of gaps
events.body: Tormod mac Sheumais, called Tormod Pinn for the speed of his hand, succeeds Gormshuil as royal chronicler and opens his own first book by copying her last list whole, striking nothing from it, so it is not lost to be rewritten by a less patient hand.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tormod Pinn

told_in.section: IV. Of the Chronicle Laid Down

events.title: The first Ros mhòr hull launched
events.body: Built on evenings and Sabbaths through a year, the yard's first hull takes the water clean at Ros mhòr, swifter than anything the southern yards have launched in a long season. Harry Marlow tells the men beside him he means to live to see the north sail hulls built with no southern guild's leave.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ros mhòr's boatyard

told_in.section: V. Of the Keel at Ros mhòr

events.title: Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill's last entry
events.body: Tormod Pinn copies into the front of his first book the last entry Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill made as chronicler, a list of what the record lacks: the northern towns' own accounts, the humans' treaties in their own tongue, and the Board's surveys. He adds nothing to it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Pinn adds his own line to the list of gaps

events.title: Tormod Pinn adds his own line to the list of gaps
events.body: Riding the southern circuit his predecessor once rode, Tormod Pinn adds beneath Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill's list of what Eachdraidh na Rìoghachd lacks a line of his own, that a gap named is worth more than a gap forgotten, and copies both into the chest that goes to an Leabharlann.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill's last entry

told_in.section: I. Of the List Copied and the Grain That Came North

events.title: Dry years at Achadh shean
events.body: Dry years come again to the country about Achadh shean, where the Long Drought settled in the humans' time. This time the council sends grain up the coal line and pays for it out of the Sloc Mòr's share. No one in the shire dies of hunger, and the chronicler records it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The maor of Achadh shean petitions early

events.title: The maor of Achadh shean petitions early
events.body: With three wells of the drove road gone brackish and a fourth dry to the stone, the maor of Siorrachd Achadh shean writes south before the second month of the dry is out rather than wait for the harvest itself to fail, and asks that a man argues with a poor harvest but a well gone to stone argues with no one.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dry years at Achadh shean

told_in.section: I. Of the List Copied and the Grain That Came North

events.title: The wells of Siorrachd Achadh shean
events.body: The maor of Siorrachd Achadh shean has twelve wells dug to the rock along the drove road, each marked with the name of the shire and of the council. Water is drawn from four of them still.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A fifth well dug dry on a dowser's word

events.title: A fifth well dug dry on a dowser's word
events.body: Of the twelve wells the maor of Achadh shean has cut along the drove road, one stands dry from the day it is dug, sited on a dowser's hazel rather than any surveyor's word, and the well-diggers own the fact afterward without much shame in the owning.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The wells of Siorrachd Achadh shean

told_in.section: I. Of the List Copied and the Grain That Came North

events.title: Grain by the coal line
events.body: The grain for Achadh shean comes from the store at Cathair fhada, and for the first time it goes by the coal line. The Rail Board charges the council for the carriage.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first wagons reach Achadh shean in the rain

events.title: The first wagons reach Achadh shean in the rain
events.body: The Cathair fhada store's grain reaches the sidings at Achadh shean by Slighe a' Ghuail on the morning the season's first proper rain falls at last, and the maor, standing in the mud he had prayed six weeks for, tells the carters the grain waited on the roof to prove it was not wanted.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Grain by the coal line

told_in.section: I. Of the List Copied and the Grain That Came North

events.title: Raiders at Baile ìseal
events.body: Raiders land near Baile ìseal on the far east coast and burn the salt-sheds of Àth bheag. The kingdom's patrol boats come two days later and find the sheds cold.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The salt-sheds of Àth bheag rebuilt

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The patrol captain's report on the two days

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh among the ash at Àth bheag

events.title: The salt-sheds of Àth bheag rebuilt
events.body: The burned salt-sheds of Àth bheag are raised again within the year, An Crùn paying a third of the cost as it once paid a third of Cuan dhearg's relief, and the salt trade limps through the interval on what the barrels spared from the fire can carry.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raiders at Baile ìseal

told_in.section: III. Of the Burning of the Salt-Sheds

events.title: The patrol captain's report on the two days
events.body: Called to answer before the shire's maor, the patrol's captain writes a report naming the distance, the wind and the hour the alarm reached his harbour; Comhairle nan Taighean-solais judges it honest, and the households of Àth bheag, hearing it read at the market cross, judge it an accounting that answers every question but the one that matters.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raiders at Baile ìseal

told_in.section: III. Of the Burning of the Salt-Sheds

events.title: Murchadh mac Coinnich's log
events.body: Murchadh mac Coinnich, keeper of Taigh-solais Baile ìseal, begins to enter in the lighthouse log every unlit ship he sees, with her heading and the hour. His logs, kept most of his life, are the fullest record of the eastern raiders in the library.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Comhairle nan Taighean-solais's inspector calls the Baile ìseal log the emptiest on the round

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh buys a second book at his own coin

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh's first full year of the unlit ships

events.title: Comhairle nan Taighean-solais's inspector calls the Baile ìseal log the emptiest on the round
events.body: Comhairle nan Taighean-solais's own inspector, checking oil against entries at Taigh-solais Baile ìseal, tells Murchadh mac Coinnich that his log is the tidiest on the eastern round and the emptiest, a remark Murchadh takes for a compliment until he comes, within the year, to hear it differently.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Murchadh mac Coinnich's log

told_in.section: II. Of the Keeper at the Point

events.title: Murchadh buys a second book at his own coin
events.body: Murchadh mac Coinnich buys, from a Muileann leathan binder a carter brings up the coast, a book of his own beside Comhairle nan Taighean-solais's, in which he means to set down what Comhairle nan Taighean-solais's own log has no line for: every ship that crosses under his light showing no lamp.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Murchadh mac Coinnich's log

told_in.section: IV. Of the Log Begun

events.title: Murchadh among the ash at Àth bheag
events.body: Once relief has come for his light, Murchadh mac Coinnich rides down to Àth bheag the second morning after the burning and stands with the ford-keepers among the wet ash and the barrel-hoops of the salt-sheds, hearing from a woman of the trade what the fire has cost.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raiders at Baile ìseal

told_in.section: III. Of the Burning of the Salt-Sheds

events.title: The pirates' names
events.body: The raiders fly no flag, and Murchadh mac Coinnich's log names their ships as the fishermen of Àth bheag name them. From his log the names pass into the royal record.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The salt-carrier names the raiders' hulls

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh's book copied fair for Eachdraidh na Rìoghachd

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh's first full year of the unlit ships

events.title: The salt-carrier names the raiders' hulls
events.body: An old salt-carrier at the Àth bheag quay gives Murchadh mac Coinnich the coast's own names for two dark hulls that have crossed under his light unlit, An Ròn Dubh for her low black run and An Fhaoileag for a habit of standing off by day and closing only with the dark.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pirates' names

told_in.section: IV. Of the Log Begun

events.title: Murchadh's book copied fair for Eachdraidh na Rìoghachd
events.body: A clerk of an Leabharlann carries Murchadh mac Coinnich's private log south, and Tormod Pinn draws the names An Ròn Dubh and An Fhaoileag into the royal record from it, crediting no better source than a keeper's own ledger and the salt-carriers of a coast the patrol once answered two days late.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pirates' names

told_in.section: IV. Of the Log Begun

events.title: The Còmhrag at its height
events.body: The Còmhrag draws its greatest crowd yet to Ceann leathan, and the fair-wardens build timber stands along three sides of the field. The champion is Ealasaid nic Coinnich of Àth ghlas, the first woman to win it. She does not fight again.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ealasaid nic Coinnich declines to defend the year's honour

events.title: Ealasaid nic Coinnich declines to defend the year's honour
events.body: Asked by the fair-wardens whether she will defend the champion's honour the following year, Ealasaid nic Coinnich tells them a thing won once stays won whether or not she stands the field a second year, and returns to her family's trade at Àth ghlas.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Còmhrag at its height

told_in.section: V. Of the Champion of Àth ghlas

events.title: Murchadh's first full year of the unlit ships
events.body: By the second an Dùbhlachd of his own keeping, Murchadh mac Coinnich's private book holds above thirty crossings, most nameless still, ruled by a straight-edge and set on the shelf beside Comhairle nan Taighean-solais's own log as the truer account of what sails the eastern water dark.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Murchadh mac Coinnich's log

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pirates' names

told_in.section: IV. Of the Log Begun

events.title: The Hawk river port of Cnoc bheag
events.body: Cnoc bheag, greatest town of the Hawk country, passes Cathair mhòr in its numbers. Its river quays take the grain of the north-central country, and its Hawk house is the richest of any order outside the capital.

events.title: Scoiltean nan Draoidhean revived
events.body: The druid schools of Flidais, silent since the humans ruled, open again. Their first question, why the vein answers some and not others, presses hard once more, for the vein itself is failing.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The old druid houses mended before the teaching

events.title: Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain's lectures
events.body: The first teacher of the revived school is Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain. She lectures in the sacred wood of Flidais near Muileann chiar in the east, where the druids last met under the humans, and opens with the school's oldest question, plainly put: why the vein answers some hands and not others.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: An old cutter's son questions Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain

events.title: The old druid houses mended before the teaching
events.body: Before a single lecture is given, villagers near Muileann chiar mend the doors and sills of the long-shut druid house with green timber and their own hands, asking no wage beyond a bench kept for them once the teaching begins.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Scoiltean nan Draoidhean revived

told_in.section: I. Of Cnoc bheag and the Waking Schools

events.title: An old cutter's son questions Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain
events.body: After her first lecture in the sacred wood, an old man whose father kept An Aois Naomh strike-books asks Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain whether she means to answer her own question before she finishes teaching it. She tells him plainly that she does not.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain's lectures

told_in.section: II. Of the Lecture in Flidais's Wood

events.title: The druid schools in Siorrachd Baile gharbh
events.body: The houses of the druid schools in Siorrachd Baile gharbh in the north-east, silent since the humans' time, open again at Baile gharbh and Àth fhada. Their teachers walk to the sacred wood to hear Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain, and walk back.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Baile gharbh teachers' first walk south

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A Baile gharbh teacher's minute of the walk

events.title: The school at Caol shean
events.body: The druid school takes a house at Caol shean, one of the great druid towns of the east, and teaches there in the wet months, when the wood is too sodden for lectures. Its students copy the census note on the coal-touched and dispute it openly.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The census line argued by lamplight at Caol shean

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Muileann dhearg hall given back to the school

events.title: The Hawk given a place
events.body: A council of the Rite at Seann Skell offers the Hawk houses of Cnoc bheag a place under the high custodian with their own order of worship. The Hawk houses take the place and keep their order. After this the quarrel is quieter. It does not end.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Òrd an t-Seabhaig's terms read a seventh time

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Pinn marks the two Dùn thais west and east

events.title: The Baile gharbh teachers' first walk south
events.body: Teachers of the reopened druid houses in Siorrachd Baile gharbh walk the better part of a week to hear Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain teach in the sacred wood before daring to open the question in their own halls, and do not miss a winter's walk after.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The druid schools in Siorrachd Baile gharbh

told_in.section: II. Of the Lecture in Flidais's Wood

events.title: The census line argued by lamplight at Caol shean
events.body: In the wet-house at Caol shean a miller's son newly come to the school asks why the census line for fuil-ghuail should be a matter no one may question, when the vein itself is questioned daily under the same roof; the argument runs past the hour the hearth is banked.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The school at Caol shean

told_in.section: III. Of the Wet House at Caol shean

events.title: The Muileann dhearg hall given back to the school
events.body: Comann nan Gualadairean' captains give the school the hall at Muileann dhearg, shut since a gallery there closed three years before, on the one condition that nothing taught in it name a living captain or gallery; the school keeps to it gladly.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The school at Caol shean

told_in.section: III. Of the Wet House at Caol shean

events.title: Òrd an t-Seabhaig's terms read a seventh time
events.body: At a council of Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail at Seann Skell on the southern coast, Àrd-choimheadaiche's clerks read Òrd an t-Seabhaig of Cnoc bheag the same settlement offered six times before; this time no witness raises the old objection, and the terms stand.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Hawk given a place

told_in.section: III. Of the Wet House at Caol shean

events.title: A Baile gharbh teacher's minute of the walk
events.body: The youngest of the Baile gharbh teachers, a woman not yet twenty on her first walk south to the sacred wood, writes of the journey in her school's own minute-book, and her school does not miss a winter's walk after.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The druid schools in Siorrachd Baile gharbh

told_in.section: II. Of the Lecture in Flidais's Wood

events.title: The north-eastern harbours
events.body: Caol chrom and Caol gharbh on the north-east coast join their harbour dues to pay for a breakwater across the strait between them. It is eight years in the building and is the longest on the island yet.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first stone of the Caol chrom breakwater

events.title: Daniel Frayne's copying school
events.body: At Muileann leathan in the north Daniel Frayne, a clerk of the Moot, teaches young Tuathaich to copy and bind books, since the guilds of that craft in the south will not take them. The bindings of Muileann leathan are found afterwards in Dia-thìrich libraries without their makers' names.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Daniel Frayne buried at Muileann leathan

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Daniel Frayne opens his bindery at Muileann leathan

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Frayne's first bindings sold south without his name

events.title: The Abhainn uaine ferries
events.body: The boat-landing at Cidhe Beag on the Abhainn uaine is licensed as a ferry, to carry passengers and small freight down the river toward the coast. The first to hold the licence is an old boatman who had worked the landing without one for forty years.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The old boatman's licence at Cidhe Beag

events.title: Daniel Frayne opens his bindery at Muileann leathan
events.body: Daniel Frayne builds a press from a mended cider-press and teaches young Tuathaich hands to fold, sew and board a book, a craft the southern guilds have never let a Tuathaich learn under their own mark; he asks no guild's leave to teach it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Daniel Frayne's copying school

told_in.section: IV. Of the Bindery, the Breakwater and the Two Dùn thais

events.title: Frayne's first bindings sold south without his name
events.body: The bindery's first plain-calf volumes, carrying no maker's name, are carried south with the wool carts and sold to Dia-thìreach households who praise the binding's neatness to Frayne's own face, none of them knowing whose pupils' hands had actually sewn the spine they hold.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Daniel Frayne's copying school

told_in.section: IV. Of the Bindery, the Breakwater and the Two Dùn thais

events.title: The first stone of the Caol chrom breakwater
events.body: Caol chrom and its neighbour across the strait lay the first stone of a shared breakwater, the longest yet built on the island, meant to close a strait that has drowned more boats in a hard winter than either shire's harbour dues could bear alone.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The north-eastern harbours

told_in.section: IV. Of the Bindery, the Breakwater and the Two Dùn thais

events.title: The old boatman's licence at Cidhe Beag
events.body: The boatman who has rowed the crossing at Cidhe Beag on the Abhainn uaine for forty years without leave asked or given is granted a licence at last by the shire's maor, more for the shire's own records than for any change in how he rows or reckons his fare.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Abhainn uaine ferries

told_in.section: IV. Of the Bindery, the Breakwater and the Two Dùn thais

events.title: Tormod Pinn marks the two Dùn thais west and east
events.body: Finding An Crùn's returns beginning to run its two towns of one name together, Tormod Pinn rules a fresh line across the royal record marking Dùn thais in the west against Dùn thais in the east, and sends word to both shires' clerks to take more care.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Hawk given a place

told_in.section: IV. Of the Bindery, the Breakwater and the Two Dùn thais

events.title: Loch chrom
events.body: The fishermen of Loch chrom, the only great lake of the island, are licensed to net its trout, which was kept for the Crown's table. Each year the Crown's table is served first.

events.title: The pillar at Cnoc chiar
events.body: Students of the druid schools try to read the pillar near Cnoc chiar by setting it beside the obelisk at Cnoc bheag and the column at Cnoc ghorm. They find signs in common and no meaning. Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain writes that the Old Ones were here and said so, and that none living can hear it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Three slates carried to Caol shean

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A mark in common on three stones

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain writes Seann-Dhaoine' sentence

events.title: Three slates carried to Caol shean
events.body: Three of Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain's students ride from the sacred wood to copy Colbh Cnoc chiar, Carragh Cnoc bheag over the town's quays and Calbh Cnoc ghorm onto separate slates, and carry them back through the rain to lay side by side.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pillar at Cnoc chiar

told_in.section: V. Of the Pillar Set Beside the Obelisk

events.title: A mark in common on three stones
events.body: Comparing the three copied slates by lamplight, the students of Caol shean find a mark like a bent reed and a straight double stroke cut on all three stones and nowhere else known to them, and no meaning in either that any among them can bring out.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pillar at Cnoc chiar

told_in.section: V. Of the Pillar Set Beside the Obelisk

events.title: Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain writes Seann-Dhaoine' sentence
events.body: Reading the three slates laid together at Caol shean, Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain writes that Seann-Dhaoine were here and said so, and that none living can hear what they said; her students copy the sentence into every school's minute-book after her.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pillar at Cnoc chiar

told_in.section: V. Of the Pillar Set Beside the Obelisk

events.title: Flood at Inis chrom
events.body: A storm tide floods the lower town of Inis chrom on the south-west coast and drowns the net-lofts and the rope-walk. The town builds both again on piles, and so they stand now.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Inis chrom's lofts rebuilt on piles

events.title: Inis chrom's lofts rebuilt on piles
events.body: After the storm tide drowns its net-lofts and rope-walk, Inis chrom does not ask An Crùn for its rebuilding. Its own carpenters raise both a second time on driven piles a fathom above the old floor, timber floated down the Abhainn ghorm from the woods above Àth gharbh, the work finished before the autumn herring.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Flood at Inis chrom

told_in.section: I. Of the Piles and the Six Schools

events.title: Cnoc leathan's schools
events.body: Cnoc leathan in the east opens a school in every one of its six parishes, paid from the shire's dues, the first shire to do so. The council asks how it paid for them and is shown the accounts.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cnoc leathan's sixth parish school

events.title: Cnoc leathan's sixth parish school
events.body: The last and smallest of Cnoc leathan's six new parish schools opens with eleven children on its benches and a teacher hired from Baile chiar. The council's clerk, sent to ask how the shire paid for six schools at once, is shown plain accounts and asks nothing further.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cnoc leathan's schools

told_in.section: I. Of the Piles and the Six Schools

events.title: Alasdair mac Ùisdein's loan
events.body: Alasdair mac Ùisdein, grandson of the first holder of the Sloc Mòr concession, borrows against his house's share to pay for a search for a second vein. The Mine Board lends its surveyors. The Crown lends its name.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Catrìona nic Neacail lent to the search

events.title: Catrìona nic Neacail lent to the search
events.body: Comhairle nam Mèinnean names eleven surveyors to Alasdair mac Ùisdein's Sireadh na Dàrna Fèithe. Catrìona nic Neacail, thirty-two, a chain-hand risen through the vein-towns, is one of them, and tells a senior surveyor riding out with her that she would rather walk ground and find nothing than be told years on that nobody looked.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Alasdair mac Ùisdein's loan

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The search for a second vein

told_in.section: II. Of the Borrowing

events.title: The druid school on the search
events.body: Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain writes to the Mine Board that the search asks the wrong question. The school has always asked why the vein answers some hands, she says, and no one has asked why there is one vein. The Board files the letter.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain's letter read a second time

events.title: Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain's letter read a second time
events.body: A clerk of Comhairle nam Mèinnean sorting the year's correspondence finds Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain's letter on the search, filed unread when it was first sent, and carries it to Catrìona nic Neacail along with Mòrag nic Coinnich's. Catrìona keeps a copy of both beside her own last entry, though she judges the school's question and Comhairle nam Mèinnean's chain answer to different masters.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The druid school on the search

told_in.section: IV. Of the Same Week

events.title: The search for a second vein
events.body: The search for a second seam of the coloured coal elsewhere on the island is costly, and finds nothing. The same search had been made in the Age of Ailean, thousands of years before, and had failed in the same way; it had been forgotten.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Catrìona nic Neacail lent to the search

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first shaft above Dùn dhearg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mòrag nic Coinnich finds An Aois Naomh roll

events.title: The first shaft above Dùn dhearg
events.body: The search's first shaft goes down above Dùn dhearg in stone that gives every hopeful sign, the diggers wagering small coin among themselves on the day the vein will show. It is judged barren within the fortnight, the first entry in a tally that will run to forty-one.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The search for a second vein

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Forty-one dry shafts

told_in.section: III. Of the Forty-One

events.title: Forty-one dry shafts
events.body: The borings of the search run from the hills above Dùn dhearg to the moors south of Baile ruadh. Forty-one shafts are sunk, and none strikes the vein. Afterwards Mòrag nic Coinnich finds in a list of the Holy Age at the library the same hills named as searched and barren.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first shaft above Dùn dhearg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The moor's own name, am Fearann Falamh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The forty-first shaft struck dry

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mòrag nic Coinnich finds An Aois Naomh roll

links.label: Leads to
links.title: An Leabharlann's copy of the old survey promised south

events.title: The moor's own name, am Fearann Falamh
events.body: An old digger of Dùn dhearg tells Catrìona nic Neacail the moor's shepherds have long called the search's ground am Fearann Falamh, meaning only that no shepherd ever found a spring there worth the digging. The name outlasts the search's own hope of it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Forty-one dry shafts

told_in.section: III. Of the Forty-One

events.title: The forty-first shaft struck dry
events.body: The last shaft of the search, sunk on the moor south of Baile ruadh through the hardest weather any of the forty had asked, strikes water at a depth no vein has ever answered. Catrìona nic Neacail writes the word barren in her own field-book a forty-first time and sits a while on the spoil-heap before riding to report it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Forty-one dry shafts

told_in.section: III. Of the Forty-One

events.title: Mòrag nic Coinnich finds An Aois Naomh roll
events.body: Cataloguing an Leabharlann's lower room, Mòrag nic Coinnich finds a Holy Age survey naming the same hills above Dùn dhearg and moors south of Baile ruadh, searched once and found barren ages before, the surveyors' own names worn from the roll. She sends Catrìona nic Neacail word the same week the forty-first shaft is closed.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The search for a second vein

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Forty-one dry shafts

told_in.section: IV. Of the Same Week

events.title: An Leabharlann's copy of the old survey promised south
events.body: Catrìona nic Neacail copies Mòrag nic Coinnich's letter into her own field-book beside her last entry and resolves to see An Aois Naomh roll sent south in copy, so that any surveyor sent to the same ground again will not have to wait on a keeper's own cataloguing to learn what the last search cost.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Forty-one dry shafts

told_in.section: IV. Of the Same Week

events.title: Sheep fall into the open shafts
events.body: On the moor south of Baile ruadh, where the ground is softest and the covering poorest, sheep begin falling into the search's open shaft-mouths before the first winter is out, three that the shire's reckoning can put a number to and likely more that no reckoning counts.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The shafts at Baile ruadh left open

told_in.section: V. Of the Fence

events.title: Dùn dhearg's claim
events.body: The town of Dùn dhearg, whose hills held a dozen of the dry shafts, claims damages from the house of Mac Ùisdein for spoiled grazing. The circuit court awards them. The house pays a third before it sells.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dùn dhearg's shepherds testify at the circuit court

events.title: Dùn dhearg's shepherds testify at the circuit court
events.body: At the circuit court's hearing of Dùn dhearg's claim, two shepherds swear that grazing spoiled by the search's spoil-heaps is lost longer than any digger reckoned, one saying he lost more lambs to the search's own open ground in two years than to wolves in ten. The court finds for the town.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dùn dhearg's claim

told_in.section: V. Of the Fence

events.title: The house of Mac Ùisdein sells half
events.body: To meet its debts the house of Mac Ùisdein sells half its share in the Sloc Mòr back to the Crown. Its stone house at Cathair mhòr is let to the Mine Board, which moves its offices there.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Mac Ùisdein stone house let to Comhairle nam Mèinnean

events.title: The Mac Ùisdein stone house let to Comhairle nam Mèinnean
events.body: Its coin thinned by the search and Dùn dhearg's damages, Taigh Mhic Ùisdein lets its stone house at Cathair mhòr, kept in the family since the first holder's day, to Comhairle nam Mèinnean, which moves its offices into it the following spring.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The house of Mac Ùisdein sells half

told_in.section: V. Of the Fence

events.title: The shafts at Baile ruadh left open
events.body: The dry shafts of the search are left open on the moors near Baile ruadh. Sheep fall into them, and one child, before the shire fences them at its own cost. The shire's claim on the house of Mac Ùisdein for the fencing is never paid.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Sheep fall into the open shafts

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The child of Baile ruadh lost to an open shaft

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile ruadh votes to fence the forty-one shafts

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A mother takes the long road at Baile ruadh

events.title: The child of Baile ruadh lost to an open shaft
events.body: A child of Baile ruadh, out after a stray lamb on ground she has walked without harm a hundred times, falls into one of the search's uncovered shafts and is not found until the day after. The parish's own book holds her name and the day, and nothing more.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The shafts at Baile ruadh left open

told_in.section: V. Of the Fence

events.title: Baile ruadh votes to fence the forty-one shafts
events.body: The shire of Baile ruadh votes to fence every one of the search's forty-one shafts at its own cost rather than wait on An Crùn, and enters a claim against Taigh Mhic Ùisdein for the fencing's cost that is never paid. The fencing goes up through the summer, post and wire round every covered mouth.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The shafts at Baile ruadh left open

told_in.section: V. Of the Fence

events.title: A mother takes the long road at Baile ruadh
events.body: The mother of the child lost in the open shaft at Baile ruadh will not walk that road again the whole of the year after, and takes the longer way round by the mill whatever the weather asks of her.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The shafts at Baile ruadh left open

told_in.section: V. Of the Fence

events.title: The Muileann dhomhain mills
events.body: The mills of Muileann dhomhain in the south-east ground grain for the vein-towns. When the vein-towns' orders fall they turn to grinding bark for the tanners. The miller-families of the town keep their mark and change their trade.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Muileann dhomhain's mills turn to bark

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A Muileann dhomhain miller answers a clerk of Comhairle nam Mèinnean

events.title: Muileann dhomhain's mills turn to bark
events.body: With the vein-towns' grain orders thinned by scarce coin, the mills of Muileann dhomhain begin grinding bark for the coast's tanners instead of grain. The miller-families keep the mark cut into their stone before any shire held a charter to license it, and change the trade under it without asking Comhairle nam Mèinnean's leave.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Muileann dhomhain mills

told_in.section: I. Of Bark and Rope and a List Alone

events.title: A Muileann dhomhain miller answers a clerk of Comhairle nam Mèinnean
events.body: Asked by a passing clerk whether it troubles her to grind bark at a wheel her family has ground grain at for four generations, the eldest of the Muileann dhomhain millers answers that a wheel does not know what is under it, and the grain will come back once the vein-towns have coin to buy it with again.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Muileann dhomhain mills

told_in.section: I. Of Bark and Rope and a List Alone

events.title: The rope-makers of Seann Tarr
events.body: The rope-makers of Seann Tarr on the north-east coast are chartered as a guild, the last guild the restored custom makes for a trade the humans had not touched. Their hemp comes from the fields about Doire uaine and Achadh naomh.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The crane walked from Seann Tarr to Àth dhearg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The rope-makers of Seann Tarr chartered

events.title: The rope-makers of Seann Tarr chartered
events.body: The restored custom charters the rope-walks of Seann Tarr as a guild, the last trade the humans never touched to be given a charter of its own. Its hemp is carted down from the fields about Doire uaine and Achadh naomh by roads older than the survey lines that have tried more than once to straighten them.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The rope-makers of Seann Tarr

told_in.section: I. Of Bark and Rope and a List Alone

events.title: Seann Tarr's chest remembered
events.body: By the shire's own rule the rope-makers' charter at Seann Tarr is kept in the shire's chest and not sent to Cathair dhearg. The shire keeper of Seann Tarr keeps a list of what the chest holds and sends the list alone.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seann Tarr's chest sends only its list

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A list is cheaper to lose than a charter

events.title: Seann Tarr's chest sends only its list
events.body: Asked to send the new rope-makers' charter south to Comhairle nam Mèinnean's own files, the shire keeper of Seann Tarr answers that the charter will stay in the shire's own chest, and sends a rider south with a list of what the chest holds and no more. No second rider is sent to ask again.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seann Tarr's chest remembered

told_in.section: I. Of Bark and Rope and a List Alone

events.title: The Circus at Inis àrsaidh
events.body: An Siorcas Siubhail Do-thuigsinn is recorded again, pitched this time on the common near Inis àrsaidh in the west. The magistrate who licenses it enters the acts as 'various' and the fee as paid.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: An Siorcas Siubhail Do-thuigsinn at Inis àrsaidh licensed as 'various'

events.title: An Siorcas Siubhail Do-thuigsinn at Inis àrsaidh licensed as 'various'
events.body: An Siorcas Siubhail Do-thuigsinn pitches again on the common near Inis àrsaidh. The magistrate who licenses its acts, unable to put a name to half of what he has watched, enters the whole of it in his book as various and the fee as paid, an entry an Leabharlann's copyists find hardest of the year to gloss.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Circus at Inis àrsaidh

told_in.section: I. Of Bark and Rope and a List Alone

events.title: A list is cheaper to lose than a charter
events.body: It is said at Seann Tarr, not without pride, that a shire which will not send its papers south need never trouble over what is done with them there, and that a list is a cheaper thing to lose than a charter.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seann Tarr's chest remembered

told_in.section: I. Of Bark and Rope and a List Alone

events.title: Ceann mhin's fish-market
events.body: Ceann mhin, the great port south-east of the capital, opens a covered fish-market over the old strand. Fish from Seann Bhral and the eastern grounds is sold there for the capital.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ceann mhin roofs its fish-market

events.title: Ceann mhin roofs its fish-market
events.body: Ceann mhin opens a covered market over its old strand for fish carried up from Seann Bhral and the eastern grounds, the first roof the port has raised over the trade. The strand's old traders grumble at first, and grumble less once a wet winter lets them keep a fire by the scales.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ceann mhin's fish-market

told_in.section: I. Of Bark and Rope and a List Alone

events.title: Edged tools banned from the Còmhrag
events.body: A fighter is killed with a hewer's pick, and the fair-wardens of Ceann leathan ban edged tools from the Còmhrag. Staves and fists are still allowed, and so the deaths go on, fewer.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Edged iron banned from Còmhrag Ceann leathan

events.title: Edged iron banned from Còmhrag Ceann leathan
events.body: After a fighter is killed at Ceann leathan with a hewer's pick carried in under a borrowed coat, the fair-wardens ban edged iron from the ring. Staves and fists are still allowed, and the dying goes on, slower, which a warden of long standing calls the whole of what the ban was ever meant to promise.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Edged tools banned from the Còmhrag

told_in.section: I. Of Bark and Rope and a List Alone

events.title: The drowned lighthouse keeper
events.body: The keeper of Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg on the south coast drowns going out to a boat aground on the reef below the light. The boat's crew are saved by his daughter, Ciorstaidh nic Artair, and she is given the keeper's warrant in his place.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Artair mac Mhurchaidh drowns off Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ciorstaidh nic Artair brings in the last of the crew

links.label: Leads to
