links.title: Artair mac Mhurchaidh buried above the light

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Comhairle nan Taighean-solais confirms Ciorstaidh nic Artair's warrant

events.title: Artair mac Mhurchaidh drowns off Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg
events.body: When a Doire shean fishing boat strikes the reef below the light in a hard south-west wind, keeper Artair mac Mhurchaidh, fifty-three, goes out alone with a rope and brings two of the four crew ashore, then goes back for the other two and does not return the third time, after above thirty years keeping that light.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The drowned lighthouse keeper

told_in.section: II. Of Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg

events.title: Ciorstaidh nic Artair brings in the last of the crew
events.body: Waking to find her father's boat gone, Ciorstaidh nic Artair, three-and-twenty, takes the second boat out along his own rope's line and finds the wreck, her father's rope still fast to it. She rows the last two of the Doire shean crew ashore herself, a boat built for a lighter woman than she then is.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The drowned lighthouse keeper

told_in.section: II. Of Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg

events.title: Artair mac Mhurchaidh buried above the light
events.body: Artair mac Mhurchaidh's body comes ashore three days after the wreck and is carried back to Tobar dhearg, to the ground above the light where every keeper before him lies. The parish register enters against his name the day, the manner, and the single word every drowning of that water is given: drowned.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The drowned lighthouse keeper

told_in.section: II. Of Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg

events.title: Comhairle nan Taighean-solais confirms Ciorstaidh nic Artair's warrant
events.body: Asked by the shire's own maor whether the daughter of a keeper who died bringing in four lives with two boats and one rope may keep the light he kept, Comhairle nan Taighean-solais at Cathair dhearg writes back within the month that she may, and enters the warrant in her name without recorded debate.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The drowned lighthouse keeper

told_in.section: II. Of Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg

events.title: Ciorstaidh nic Artair's reef mark
events.body: Ciorstaidh nic Artair has an iron post set on the reef below Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg, painted and hung with a bell. While she keeps the light no boat goes aground there.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The reef post raised by subscription

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Comhairle nan Taighean-solais's engineer approves the reef bell

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Two Seann Vell masons set the reef post

events.title: The reef post raised by subscription
events.body: Ciorstaidh nic Artair has an iron post sunk into the reef at low water, painted the red of danger marked and known, and hung with a bell cast at Muileann chiar. Half the cost comes from Comhairle nan Taighean-solais's purse and half from a purse the fishing families of Doire shean and Tobar dhearg make up between them.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ciorstaidh nic Artair's reef mark

told_in.section: III. Of the Bell in Fog

events.title: Comhairle nan Taighean-solais's engineer approves the reef bell
events.body: Comhairle nan Taighean-solais's engineer walks the reef at low water and pronounces the post sound and the casting good. Asked whether she means to add clockwork to strike the hour as well as the danger, Ciorstaidh nic Artair answers that a man wanting the hour has a tide table and two eyes, and needs neither bell nor clockwork for that.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ciorstaidh nic Artair's reef mark

told_in.section: III. Of the Bell in Fog

events.title: Mary Coyle lays down the chair
events.body: Mary Coyle lays down the chair of the Moot at Caol mhòr. Daniel Frayne of Muileann leathan follows her, the first speaker born after the Severance.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The reef bell first rings in fog

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mary Coyle lays down the chair of Tional nan Tuathach

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Daniel Frayne chosen speaker of Tional nan Tuathach

events.title: The reef bell first rings in fog
events.body: In a fog thick enough to hide the light itself, the bell on its post rings of its own weight as the sea moves it, and every boat working that stretch of coast steers home by the sound alone. No boat goes aground on the reef below Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg that year, nor in any year Ciorstaidh nic Artair keeps the light after.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Mary Coyle lays down the chair

told_in.section: III. Of the Bell in Fog

events.title: Mary Coyle lays down the chair of Tional nan Tuathach
events.body: After two-and-twenty years in the chair, Mary Coyle lays it down at Caol mhòr, speaking of the register of the western pits' dead and maimed her hand began and Slighe a' Ghuail her petitions never once moved south of Àth leathan, and names before Tional nan Tuathach rises the man she asks it to choose after her.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Mary Coyle lays down the chair

told_in.section: IV. Of the Chair Laid Down

events.title: Daniel Frayne chosen speaker of Tional nan Tuathach
events.body: Daniel Frayne of Muileann leathan, who bound books for the north's schools when the southern guilds would not take a Tuathaich name, is chosen speaker without a voice raised against him: the first to have been born after An Dealachadh closed, and Mary Coyle's own right hand in the chair for above ten years before it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Mary Coyle lays down the chair

told_in.section: IV. Of the Chair Laid Down

events.title: The Fèill's northern day
events.body: The court of the fair at Muileann òg sets aside one day of the fair for goods from the northern shires. They are still sold through Dia-thìrich factors, but under the northern makers' own marks. It is the first time a Tuathaich name is written on anything sold there.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The grey twill first on the pole

events.title: Two Seann Vell masons set the reef post
events.body: Two masons brought up from Seann Vell drive and cement Ciorstaidh nic Artair's iron post into the reef below Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg, working only the hour either side of the ebb for the better part of a month.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ciorstaidh nic Artair's reef mark

told_in.section: III. Of the Bell in Fog

events.title: The grey twill first on the pole
events.body: Daniel Frayne, six months in Tional nan Tuathach's chair, watches the first cloth of the fair's northern day go up on its pole at Muileann òg: a grey twill of Doire ghlas dyed with the shire's own bark, with a single white thread at the selvedge.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Fèill's northern day

told_in.section: I. Of the Fair's Northern Day

events.title: The Tuathaich marks at the fair
events.body: The first northern mark sold under its own name at the fair is the cloth of the weavers of Doire ghlas, a grey twill with a white thread at the selvedge. The southern weavers of Baile chiar begin to weave a white thread into their own.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Doire ghlas weaver's daughter sews by lantern

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile chiar's weavers name their own thread pale

events.title: The Doire ghlas weaver's daughter sews by lantern
events.body: At the fair's close on its first northern day, a Doire ghlas weaver's daughter left minding her mother's stall sews a second white thread into an unsold bolt after the buyers have gone. Asked why she troubles with it unwatched, she says the mark goes in whether anyone buys it or not, since a thread sewn only for show is no mark at all.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Tuathaich marks at the fair

told_in.section: I. Of the Fair's Northern Day

events.title: Baile chiar's weavers name their own thread pale
events.body: Rather than claim An Snàthainn Geal already spoken for, the weavers of Baile chiar work a grey scarcely darker than the wool into the selvedge of their own finer bolts. An old weaver tells Daniel Frayne, who asks why the south troubles to copy a northern habit, that she has woven forty years without her name on a bolt and does not mean to die without it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Tuathaich marks at the fair

told_in.section: I. Of the Fair's Northern Day

events.title: The Depletion laid bare
events.body: The quiet note of the survey in SE 26 is now an open trouble. The last unworked stretches of the vein are found, and they are smaller than any wish to own.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Catrìona nic Neacail begins the one sheet

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A concession-holder asks the sheet a plain question

events.title: Catrìona nic Neacail begins the one sheet
events.body: Catrìona nic Neacail, a surveyor of Comhairle nam Mèinnean sixteen years standing, begins drawing every stretch of the true vein still unopened onto a single leaf, working outward through Comhairle nam Mèinnean's own scattered rolls a shire at a time and riding to settle every ground the rolls disagree on.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Depletion laid bare

told_in.section: II. Of the One Sheet

events.title: Catrìona nic Neacail's map
events.body: Catrìona nic Neacail, surveyor-general of the Mine Board, publishes the map of the vein's last unworked stretches. It fits on one sheet. Within the year she gives up her post and goes to teach at the druid school at Caol shean.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A concession-holder asks the sheet a plain question

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Catrìona nic Neacail named surveyor-general

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Duilleag na Fèithe hung on the chamber wall

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Catrìona nic Neacail resigns the surveyor-general's office

events.title: A concession-holder asks the sheet a plain question
events.body: A concession-holder of four generations' standing stands before the finished sheet the better part of an hour, then asks Catrìona nic Neacail plainly whether the red marked over his own family's ground means ten years or thirty, having daughters to settle and no wish to be told later that Comhairle nam Mèinnean had always known and never troubled to colour it in.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Depletion laid bare

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Catrìona nic Neacail's map

told_in.section: II. Of the One Sheet

events.title: Catrìona nic Neacail named surveyor-general
events.body: Comhairle nam Mèinnean names Catrìona nic Neacail surveyor-general, an office left empty three years for want of anyone troubling to ask what it was for, until her one-sheet map of the vein's last unworked stretches made plain that somebody ought to answer for the whole of what it showed. She is the youngest to hold it in living memory.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Catrìona nic Neacail's map

told_in.section: II. Of the One Sheet

events.title: Duilleag na Fèithe hung on the chamber wall
events.body: Catrìona nic Neacail publishes Duilleag na Fèithe in an Dùbhlachd in the plainest way Comhairle nam Mèinnean knows, hanging it on the wall of its own chamber at Cathair mhòr, where every surveyor, clerk and concession-holder who comes can stand before it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Catrìona nic Neacail's map

told_in.section: II. Of the One Sheet

events.title: Iain Mapa's survey found
events.body: Among the Board's files Catrìona nic Neacail finds Iain Mapa's survey of thirty years before, which shows the same thinning she has just measured. She sends a copy to the library, with a note of when the Board received it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Two surveys read side by side

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Catrìona nic Neacail's visit to Muileann chiar

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ruairidh the cellar boy

events.title: Two surveys read side by side
events.body: Catrìona nic Neacail sits late at Comhairle nam Mèinnean's own table beneath her own sheet, reading her map and Iain Mapa's thirty-year-old survey side by side by lamplight, the same failing ground marked out in the same terms three decades apart, and cannot say which survey troubles her more, the one that found the truth or the one believed too late to matter.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain Mapa's survey found

told_in.section: III. Of the Press at Cathair mhòr

events.title: Catrìona nic Neacail's visit to Muileann chiar
events.body: Catrìona nic Neacail rides east to Muileann chiar and sits with Iain mac Ruairidh, three-and-sixty and failing, in what proves his last spring. He shows her his own copy of his old survey with Comhairle nam Mèinnean's receipt still pinned to it, and asks whether the school at Caol shean still keeps its old question about the vein.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain Mapa's survey found

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain Mapa dies

told_in.section: IV. Of Muileann chiar

events.title: Iain Mapa dies
events.body: Iain mac Ruairidh, called Iain Mapa, dies at Muileann chiar, where the Board sent him. His own copy of his survey is found among his papers with the Board's receipt pinned to it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Catrìona nic Neacail's visit to Muileann chiar

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Mapa buried by Comann an Airgid

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mòr nic Dhòmhnaill sends her husband's papers south

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Mapa dies at his workbench

events.title: Iain Mapa buried by Comann an Airgid
events.body: Comann an Airgid of Muileann chiar, which had paid Iain mac Ruairidh's small pension ten years, buries him with an ounce of its own refined silver laid beside him, its master saying over him that he had gone into more of the mountain's dark than any three men living and had never once come up lying about what he found there.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain Mapa dies

told_in.section: V. Of the Bell at Caol shean

events.title: Mòr nic Dhòmhnaill sends her husband's papers south
events.body: Going through her husband's papers, Mòr nic Dhòmhnaill finds the folded survey with Comhairle nam Mèinnean's old receipt still pinned to it and sends the whole of it to Leabharlann Muileann chaol, writing only that he had asked more than once it not be lost a second time, and that she knew no safer place to send it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain Mapa dies

told_in.section: V. Of the Bell at Caol shean

events.title: Muileann dhearg empties
events.body: In a few years Muileann dhearg loses a third of its households to the ports. Its druid hall is shut, and its bell sold to the school at Caol shean, where it rings for lectures still.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Muileann dhearg's maor counts the empty houses

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Fèidh hall's last teacher locks its door

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Muileann dhearg bell rings Catrìona's first lecture

events.title: Muileann dhearg's maor counts the empty houses
events.body: Muileann dhearg's maor keeps a count of houses left empty as families leave for the ports and the southern yards, a tally kept at first from ordinary habit and then from something nearer alarm, running within three years to above sixty within the shire's own walls.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Muileann dhearg empties

told_in.section: V. Of the Bell at Caol shean

events.title: The Fèidh hall's last teacher locks its door
events.body: The last teacher of Muileann dhearg's Fèidh hall, given back to Scoiltean nan Draoidhean not ten years before, locks its door herself for want of a congregation left to keep it and carries the key to the maor's own house rather than leave it with no one.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Muileann dhearg empties

told_in.section: V. Of the Bell at Caol shean

events.title: Ceann leathan's coal quays idle
events.body: Coal-ships wait at Ceann leathan for cargoes that come in half-loads. The harbour dues fall by half, and the fair-wardens raise the gate-price of the Còmhrag to make it up.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ceann leathan raises Còmhrag Ceann leathan's gate-price

events.title: Ruairidh the cellar boy
events.body: A clerk's boy of twelve who has fetched bundles in Comhairle nam Mèinnean's own cellar at Cathair mhòr for three years tells Catrìona nic Neacail she is the first to ask him to read a label aloud rather than simply hand a bundle across. He helps her keep the tally of the week's search among the old presses.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain Mapa's survey found

told_in.section: III. Of the Press at Cathair mhòr

events.title: Catrìona nic Neacail resigns the surveyor-general's office
events.body: Within the year of finding Iain Mapa's old survey, Catrìona nic Neacail resigns as surveyor-general, Comhairle nam Mèinnean's own minute recording it in four flat lines, and asks a place teaching at Scoiltean nan Draoidhean at Caol shean, judging the mountain's own answers now the only lesson in her trade worth the passing on.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Catrìona nic Neacail's map

told_in.section: V. Of the Bell at Caol shean

events.title: Ceann leathan raises Còmhrag Ceann leathan's gate-price
events.body: With the harbour dues at Ceann leathan fallen by half as coal-ships wait for cargoes that come in half loaded, the fair-wardens, whose town lives as much off the coal trade as off the yearly melee, raise the gate-price of Còmhrag Ceann leathan to make up what the quay no longer earns.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ceann leathan's coal quays idle

told_in.section: V. Of the Bell at Caol shean

events.title: The Muileann dhearg bell rings Catrìona's first lecture
events.body: Catrìona nic Neacail gives her first lecture at Caol shean in the same wood where Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain once first put the old question to her students, and the bell taken down from Muileann dhearg's shut hall, hung now in the school's own tower, is rung for the first time to call the school in.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Muileann dhearg empties

told_in.section: V. Of the Bell at Caol shean

events.title: Iain Mapa dies at his workbench
events.body: Iain mac Ruairidh dies at his own workbench at Muileann chiar in the first days of an Cèitean, not a fortnight after Catrìona nic Neacail's visit; Mòr finds him in the evening with small objects laid out before him in an order only he had understood.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain Mapa dies

told_in.section: V. Of the Bell at Caol shean

events.title: Baile Mòr dhomhain's market
events.body: As the trade of the coal-towns falls away, Baile Mòr dhomhain in the northern hills becomes the market for the wool and hides of the hill country. For two years together its market day draws more carts than the fair at Muileann òg.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Daniel Frayne notes the gaps at Muileann òg

events.title: Daniel Frayne notes the gaps at Muileann òg
events.body: A wool-buyer at Tional nan Tuathach's own table tells Daniel Frayne that Fèill Muileann òg now stands with gaps between its tents where none stood before, the fair's own wardens filling them each year with a wider aisle rather than own that the crowd has thinned.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Baile Mòr dhomhain's market

told_in.section: I. Of the Market that Passed the Fair

events.title: Mairead crowned
events.body: Eòghan's reign ends in the decade that the Depletion becomes known to all. Mairead inherits a kingdom whose founding wealth is plainly failing, for the first time since the restoration.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The old die broken at Cathair dhearg

events.title: The old die broken at Cathair dhearg
events.body: With Mairead crowned, the die that struck Eòghan's own likeness on Bonn na Rìoghachd is broken at Cathair dhearg by the mint's custom, the old coin kept good until the new is struck in number enough to answer for it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Mairead crowned

told_in.section: I. Of the Market that Passed the Fair

events.title: The Hewers bind no apprentices
events.body: For the first time since its charter the Guild of Hewers binds no new apprentices. Its masters vote to keep the rolls open to the sons and daughters of members only.

events.title: Agnes Pike dies
events.body: Agnes Pike, who opened the byre school at Doire ghlas in the fifteenth year, dies at seven-and-seventy; Daniel Frayne, reading Muileann shean's letter for primers that season, remembers her telling him that a trade a man carries in his own head weighs nothing on the road.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Muileann shean's school of hewers

told_in.section: I. Of the Market that Passed the Fair

events.title: Muileann shean's school of hewers
events.body: Muileann shean in the north opens a school for the sons and daughters of hewers who will not be bound, and teaches them to read, reckon and survey. Most of its first pupils go to the ports.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Agnes Pike dies

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Daniel Frayne binds primers for Muileann shean

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Muileann shean's benches pass thirty

events.title: Daniel Frayne binds primers for Muileann shean
events.body: Asked for primers by Muileann shean's own maor, Daniel Frayne binds forty copies of a reading-book at his own bench at Muileann leathan and sends them north on the first cart with room, the forms unchanged since he first set the type twenty years before.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Muileann shean's school of hewers

told_in.section: I. Of the Market that Passed the Fair

events.title: Muileann shean's benches pass thirty
events.body: The school Muileann shean opened for hewers' children the Guild will not bind grows within the year from eleven pupils to above thirty, though three of the first eleven have already gone south to hire themselves out as chain-hands in the ports.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Muileann shean's school of hewers

told_in.section: I. Of the Market that Passed the Fair

events.title: The Doire ghlas mills
events.body: Wool mills are built at Doire ghlas with the Moot's money, the first works in the north that owe nothing to the vein. The Rail Board refuses their cloth, until a ruling of the circuit court at Seann Bhral compels it to carry any goods that pay the rate.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The binders' reckoning

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first bolt off the Doire ghlas looms

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn refuses the first wagon

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first Doire ghlas bale rides Slighe a' Ghuail

events.title: The first bolt off the Doire ghlas looms
events.body: The wool mills raised at Doire ghlas with Tional nan Tuathach's own coin turn their first bolt, a grey twill with a white thread at the selvedge, and the overseer writes to Caol mhòr that it is better cloth than the south's own factors reckoned a northern loom could turn out.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Doire ghlas mills

told_in.section: II. Of the Doire ghlas Bolt and the Suit

events.title: Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn refuses the first wagon
events.body: Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's factors at Àth leathan, the railhead nearest the north, refuse to carry the Doire ghlas mill's first wagon-load south to Muileann òg, giving no reason beyond Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's own long custom of judging for itself what the line will carry.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Doire ghlas mills

told_in.section: II. Of the Doire ghlas Bolt and the Suit

events.title: Tional nan Tuathach brings its suit to Seann Bhral
events.body: Daniel Frayne rides west to the circuit court at Seann Bhral with the mill's ledgers and Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's letter of refusal, asking Ruairidh mac Phàdraig to rule whether a carrier chartered by An Crùn may refuse one people's cargo and take another's.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Seann Bhral ruling

told_in.section: II. Of the Doire ghlas Bolt and the Suit

events.title: The Seann Bhral ruling
events.body: Ruairidh mac Phàdraig, circuit justice at Seann Bhral, rules that the Rail Board is a carrier of the Crown and must carry for any who pay. It is the first ruling the Moot wins in a Dia-thìreach court. The Board appeals, and the council lets the appeal lapse.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tional nan Tuathach brings its suit to Seann Bhral

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The charter read clause by clause at Seann Bhral

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first Doire ghlas bale rides Slighe a' Ghuail

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The council lets Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's appeal lapse

events.title: The charter read clause by clause at Seann Bhral
events.body: When Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's factor argues at Seann Bhral that Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's rails answer to a different clause of its charter than its carts, Ruairidh mac Phàdraig has the whole charter read aloud clause by clause, and no clause is found that names the rails apart.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Seann Bhral ruling

told_in.section: II. Of the Doire ghlas Bolt and the Suit

events.title: The Crown's share of the Sloc Mòr
events.body: The Crown buys the last working shafts of the house of Mac Ùisdein at the Sloc Mòr and leaves the house its share in the spoil and the quarry. Thenceforth the Board works the vein in the Crown's name alone.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Word of Catrìona nic Neacail's going

events.title: Word of Catrìona nic Neacail's going
events.body: A clerk of Comhairle nam Mèinnean's notice of the Mac Ùisdein sale reaches Caol mhòr with a passing word that the surveyor who drew the search's last sheet has resigned her post to teach at Caol shean, a name Daniel Frayne knows only at second hand.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Crown's share of the Sloc Mòr

told_in.section: III. Of the Copper and the Last Shafts

events.title: The copper at Àth fhiadhaich
events.body: Copper is found in the hills behind Àth fhiadhaich in the eastern hills. The Board opens a working with men laid off from the Sloc Mòr. It pays wages. It is not the vein, and the town's Seann Spioradan house gives it no blessing.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mary Coyle dies at Caol mhòr

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mary Coyle buried near Walter Hale

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mary Coyle's sheet kept in Tional nan Tuathach's chest

events.title: The first Doire ghlas bale rides Slighe a' Ghuail
events.body: A year after the ruling, Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's own factor at Àth leathan weighs the first Doire ghlas bale onto the wagon without comment, the same weight given any cargo that pays the rate, and Daniel Frayne rides down to see it loaded.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Seann Bhral ruling

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Doire ghlas mills

told_in.section: III. Of the Copper and the Last Shafts

events.title: The council lets Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's appeal lapse
events.body: Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's appeal against Breith Seann Bhral lies on the council's table a winter and a spring and is let lapse in the summer, the council's minute noting only that the matter was not reached in the session's business.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Seann Bhral ruling

told_in.section: II. Of the Doire ghlas Bolt and the Suit

events.title: Mary Coyle dies at Caol mhòr
events.body: Mary Coyle, speaker of Tional nan Tuathach from the thirty-third year to the fifty-fifth, dies at Caol mhòr in the second week of an t-Iuchar at nine-and-seventy, having asked that nothing be read over her but the names.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The copper at Àth fhiadhaich

told_in.section: IV. Of the Widows' Bench

events.title: Mary Coyle buried near Walter Hale
events.body: Mary Coyle is laid in Walter Hale's ground, a little lower on the slope within sight of Tional nan Tuathach's house, and the priest reads over her only the eleven drowned of Cuan bheag, the widows of the bench by the door and her own name; three Ros mhòr men who sailed with her to Seann Bhral bring the tiller of her boat.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The copper at Àth fhiadhaich

told_in.section: IV. Of the Widows' Bench

events.title: Mary Coyle's sheet kept in Tional nan Tuathach's chest
events.body: Tional nan Tuathach votes without a count that the sheet of the eleven drowned and the widows after them, given it by Mary Coyle's family, be kept in its own chest beside Clàr nan Leòn with the space beneath the last name left empty; no notice of her death goes south.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The copper at Àth fhiadhaich

told_in.section: IV. Of the Widows' Bench

events.title: Àth fhiadhaich's copper-town
events.body: The copper workings at Àth fhiadhaich draw miners from the failing vein-towns. The town builds a new street for them and names it for the Sloc Mòr, and the Seann Spioradan house there speaks against the name.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The street named for An Sloc Mòr

events.title: The street named for An Sloc Mòr
events.body: Miners settled on Àth fhiadhaich's new street carry small lumps of coal from An Sloc Mòr's own upper galleries among their goods, keeping them for the plain fact of the carrying rather than for any use, while Na Seann Spioradan' keeper tells the council a street named for another town's mountain risks forgetting the ground it stands on.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Àth fhiadhaich's copper-town

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: I. Of the Street Named for the Pit

events.title: Dubhan begins his experiments
events.body: Dubhan makes his first attempts to draw a fuel to stand in the coal's place from the waste of the mines. They fail, and little is set down of them.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dubhan's first working set down

events.title: Dubhan's first working set down
events.body: Tormod Pinn enters a single sentence in the day-book on a report from the north, that a young man there has made trials at drawing a fuel from the waste of the mines and that they have come to nothing; he writes no more of it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dubhan begins his experiments

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: I. Of the Street Named for the Pit

events.title: The Sloc Mòr's pumps
events.body: The lowest galleries of the Sloc Mòr are let flood, for the pumps cost more to run than the coal beneath is worth. The Board's minute calls it a pause.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The last pump drawn out

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first pump goes down Slighe a' Ghuail

events.title: The last pump drawn out
events.body: Tormod Pinn rides to Achadh dhomhain and finds An Sloc Mòr's lowest galleries eleven fathoms under water, the pumps cold on Comhairle nam Mèinnean's own order; the overseer there has kept the order's own slip folded in his coat since the turn of the season, as though he expected someday to need to prove it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Sloc Mòr's pumps

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: II. Of the Galleries Let Go

events.title: The first pump goes down Slighe a' Ghuail
events.body: The first of An Sloc Mòr's three great pumps goes south under canvas on a flat wagon from a siding above Achadh dhomhain, bound for the new dry dock at Seann Bhral in the south; Tormod Pinn watches it pass and sets down that a pump goes where the water is and cares no more for the ground it served than a bolt of cloth.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Sloc Mòr's pumps

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pumps sold

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: II. Of the Galleries Let Go

events.title: The pumps sold
events.body: The Board sells the great pumps of the Sloc Mòr to the harbour at Seann Bhral in the south, where they drain the new dry dock. In the next generation they are the only engines of the vein still at work.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first pump goes down Slighe a' Ghuail

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The third pump follows and six men are found other work

links.label: Leads to
links.title: An Sloc Mòr's pumps drain the dock at Seann Bhral

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A coal-ship first stands in the Seann Bhral dock

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The dock's return filed under the harbour

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Achadh dhomhain overseer signs his name

events.title: The third pump follows and six men are found other work
events.body: The overseer at Achadh dhomhain writes that the third and last pump has gone to Seann Bhral in the south after the second, and that the six men who tended the three between them have been found work on the galleries still above water, a thing Comhairle nam Mèinnean's own notice calls no loss to any household.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pumps sold

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: II. Of the Galleries Let Go

events.title: The maor of Baile dhomhain writes of the crossing
events.body: A shire's maor writes to Comhairle nam Mèinnean of stock lost along Imrich nam Pantar near Baile dhomhain, a loss too large for wolves and weather; Comhairle nam Mèinnean's clerk, having no ledger fit to hold it, sends the letter on to an Leabharlann.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The panthers cross the south-west

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: IV. Of Imrich nam Pantar

events.title: The panthers cross the south-west
events.body: A great host of panthers crosses the south-west near Baile dhomhain. For a month the herders lose stock. Tormod Pinn writes it down as a thing named in the lists of the Holy Age and not seen in living memory.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The maor of Baile dhomhain writes of the crossing

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The old list of An Aois Naomh opened again

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The herders keep Imrich nam Pantar

events.title: The old list of An Aois Naomh opened again
events.body: Tormod Pinn sets the maor's letter beside a Library list from the days of An Aois Naomh naming the years the panthers crossed before, an interval longer than any living herder's working life, and writes the crossing's entry longer than any other that year.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The panthers cross the south-west

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Imrich nam Pantar in the chronicle

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: IV. Of Imrich nam Pantar

events.title: The herders keep Imrich nam Pantar
events.body: The herders of the south-west drive their flocks off the old road beforehand and keep the crossing as a season of watching, losing fewer beasts in the end than the first week's count had feared, though more than an ordinary year costs them.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The panthers cross the south-west

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: IV. Of Imrich nam Pantar

events.title: The hides of Baile ghorm
events.body: Tanners at Baile ghorm on the south-west coast buy the hides of the panthers the herders kill, and their trade outlasts the crossing by ten years. Saddles of panther-skin from Baile ghorm are sold at the fair at Muileann òg under the town's mark.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile ghorm's tanners buy the hides

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Panther-skins first at the fair

events.title: Baile ghorm's tanners buy the hides
events.body: Buyers from Baile ghorm ride up into the hills within the fortnight to take the hides of panthers the herders' dogs and spears have brought down, paying a price the herders judge fair for a skin they have no other use for.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hides of Baile ghorm

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: IV. Of Imrich nam Pantar

events.title: Panther-skins first at the fair
events.body: Fèill Muileann òg sees, for the first time in any chronicler's memory, saddles and belts of panther-hide sold under the Baile ghorm mark, the southern buyers taken by surprise enough that the mark's own price doubles twice before the fair is out.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hides of Baile ghorm

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: IV. Of Imrich nam Pantar

events.title: Imrich nam Pantar in the chronicle
events.body: Tormod Pinn's entry on the panthers is the longest in his book for that year. He sets it beside the list of the Holy Age, and notes that the old list names the year after the panthers as a hungry one.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The old list of An Aois Naomh opened again

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod strikes through his own note

events.title: Muileann mhin halves its lamp-making
events.body: The lamp-makers of Muileann mhin halve their making for want of coal to fire their forges properly, the coal reaching the town thinner and dearer each season An Sloc Mòr's galleries give less of it up.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The coal-lamp shortage

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: V. Of the Lent Lamps and the Yard at Muileann chrom

events.title: An Sloc Mòr's pumps drain the dock at Seann Bhral
events.body: The three great pumps of An Sloc Mòr, set on a bed of masonry at the head of the new dry dock at Seann Bhral in the south, pump it dry for the first time on the ninth day after the third is fired.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pumps sold

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: III. Of the Dry Dock at Seann Bhral

events.title: A coal-ship first stands in the Seann Bhral dock
events.body: The first hull stood dry in the new dock at Seann Bhral is a coal-ship out of Ceann leathan with her keel sprung on the bar; by the year's end eleven hulls have stood in it, and the town's shipwrights raise a shed over its head.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pumps sold

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: III. Of the Dry Dock at Seann Bhral

events.title: The dock's return filed under the harbour
events.body: Tormod Pinn enters Seann Bhral's return of the dock in Eachdraidh na Rìoghachd without a line of his own, copies into its margin the names the Achadh dhomhain men used among themselves for the three engines, and asks that the return be filed under the harbour and not under Comhairle nam Mèinnean.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pumps sold

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: III. Of the Dry Dock at Seann Bhral

events.title: The Achadh dhomhain overseer signs his name
events.body: The overseer at Achadh dhomhain writes to Tormod Pinn that the second pump has followed the first to Seann Bhral and the third stands ready, and that the six men who tended them have been found work on the galleries above water; he signs his own name to it this time rather than none.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pumps sold

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: II. Of the Galleries Let Go

events.title: The coal-lamp shortage
events.body: The lamp-makers of Muileann mhin halve their making, for want of coal to burn in the lamps they make. Shaft-lamps are lent from pit to pit, and the guild's minute-book records who lent to whom.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The first dubhan pit-lamps of Muileann mhin

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Muileann mhin halves its lamp-making

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Guild's lending-book

events.title: The Guild's lending-book
events.body: Comann nan Gualadairean keeps a plain minute-book at its hall for shaft-lamps lent from pit to pit, and Tormod Pinn, sending for a copy of its first year, finds more names entered against debts than against repayments, a dry column that tells the vein's own thinning more plainly than any letter of Comhairle nam Mèinnean.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The coal-lamp shortage

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: V. Of the Lent Lamps and the Yard at Muileann chrom

events.title: The yard families stop the trains
events.body: The yard families at Muileann chrom stop the coal trains for three days over a cut wage, putting forward as their spokesman Dòmhnall Ruadh mac Ailein, one-and-forty, whose father laid the yard's first rail; a Tuathaich minister there keeps his own book of the families' grievances.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Unrest at Muileann chrom

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: V. Of the Lent Lamps and the Yard at Muileann chrom

events.title: Unrest at Muileann chrom
events.body: The yard families at Muileann chrom stop the coal trains for three days over cut wages. On the fourth day the Rail Board settles; on the fifth it dismisses eleven men.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The yard families stop the trains

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn settles and dismisses eleven

events.title: Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn settles and dismisses eleven
events.body: Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's factor restores the old wage on the third day and the trains run again on the fourth; on the fifth Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's own notice names eleven men dismissed for their part in the stopping, Dòmhnall Ruadh mac Ailein among them, the settlement and the dismissal arriving from the same hand in the same week.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Unrest at Muileann chrom

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: V. Of the Lent Lamps and the Yard at Muileann chrom

events.title: Cathair fhada's granaries want a second storey
events.body: The maor of Cathair fhada writes to Muileann chaol that the year's harvest has proved thicker than any since before Sireadh na Dàrna Fèithe was spoken of, granaries built for a lean year now wanting a second storey to hold it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hungry year that was not

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: VI. Of the Strike-Through

events.title: The hungry year that was not
events.body: The harvest after the panthers' crossing is good across the south. Tormod Pinn records it and strikes through his own note of the year before.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cathair fhada's granaries want a second storey

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod strikes through his own note

events.title: Tormod strikes through his own note
events.body: Tormod Pinn draws a line through his own entry naming a hungry year to follow the panthers' crossing, leaving the words legible beneath it and writing that the harvest proved thick rather than thin, since a chronicle owes its readers its wrong guesses as plainly as its right ones.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hungry year that was not

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Imrich nam Pantar in the chronicle

told_in.book: Of the Pumps and the Panthers
told_in.section: VI. Of the Strike-Through

events.title: The third census after the Severance
events.body: For the first time in the Rìoghachd the numbers of the people are published openly. It is a small token of openness, and nothing else is changed.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Census clerks come north for a count

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tional nan Tuathach's figures given to the census clerks

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Frayne's private book notes the asking

events.title: Census clerks come north for a count
events.body: Two census clerks ride to Caol mhòr, the first southern office to ask Tional nan Tuathach for its own count of its own people rather than take none, the shire's own maor having told the surveyor-general no clerk had yet gone north.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The third census after the Severance

told_in.section: I. Of the Clerks Who Came for the Figures

events.title: Tional nan Tuathach's figures given to the census clerks
events.body: Daniel Frayne gives the visiting clerks Tional nan Tuathach's own count, kept every third year since the room was opened, along with the school and vigil registers, and offers to swear to the figures before a justice if the council should ask it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The third census after the Severance

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh's first foot-note

told_in.section: I. Of the Clerks Who Came for the Figures

events.title: Frayne's private book notes the asking
events.body: Daniel Frayne writes the day's giving into his own private book, judging it worth the keeping that Tional nan Tuathach had, for once, been asked for its figures rather than merely tolerated in the giving of them.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The third census after the Severance

told_in.section: I. Of the Clerks Who Came for the Figures

events.title: The figures read at the Moot
events.body: The published figures are read aloud at the Moot at Caol mhòr. They show the northern towns at about half the Dia-thìrich measure in every column the clerks chose to take. The Moot's minute says only: 'Now written.'

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A young clerk asks what the two words mean

events.title: A young clerk asks what the two words mean
events.body: Walking out of the room into the frost, a junior clerk asks Daniel Frayne whether the minute's two words oblige the south to answer for what it has printed; Frayne tells him a fact set down is not a promise kept, but cannot be unprinted either.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The figures read at the Moot

told_in.section: II. Of the Reading and the Two Words

events.title: The count of the touched
events.body: The published census, like the first, has a line for the coal-touched. It gives a number and nothing more. Tormod Pinn copies it into the chronicle without comment, as Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill did for the first.

events.title: The census in the Stone's shires
events.body: In the shires of Òrd na Cloiche in the south-west the houses of the Stone publish for the first time their own count of their people beside the kingdom's. The two agree within a hundred.

events.title: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh
events.body: Tormod Pinn dies at his desk at Muileann chaol. Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh becomes royal chronicler. She is the first to add at the foot of each year a note of what the record could not learn.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Pinn buried at Muileann chaol

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh's first morning at the desk

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Pinn found at his desk

events.title: Tormod Pinn buried at Muileann chaol
events.body: Tormod Pinn, chronicler nine-and-seventy years old, is buried in the small ground behind an Leabharlann among every keeper and chronicler the house has kept since Ailean Leabhar; Mòrag nic Coinnich speaks over him that he kept the list honest and struck nothing from it unearned.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh

told_in.section: III. Of Tormod Pinn's Last Winter

events.title: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh's first morning at the desk
events.body: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh, chosen from an Leabharlann's own senior clerks, tells the house on her first morning as chronicler that she means to change nothing of the desk's hours, only its habit of silence where the record itself keeps none.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh

told_in.section: III. Of Tormod Pinn's Last Winter

events.title: The Hawk houses' registers
events.body: The Hawk houses of Siorrachd Ros gheal send their birth-rolls to the library for the first time, on condition that they be filed under Òrd an t-Seabhaig and not under Òrd Bhrìde. Mòrag nic Coinnich agrees.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A Ros gheal carter waits in an Leabharlann's yard

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mòrag's three lines to Òrd an t-Seabhaig

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A paper filed under its sender's name

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A fourth coffer from Ros gheal

events.title: Tormod Pinn found at his desk
events.body: Tormod Pinn is found dead at his desk at Muileann chaol on a morning in an t-Sultain, the year's returns open under his hand and his pen laid down beside them; the clerks write his age, nine-and-seventy, in the margin of his last page, the only line of his tenure he did not write himself.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh

told_in.section: III. Of Tormod Pinn's Last Winter

events.title: A Ros gheal carter waits in an Leabharlann's yard
events.body: The carter who brings the three iron-bound coffers of the Ros gheal Òrd an t-Seabhaig' birth-rolls to Muileann chaol waits the whole of an afternoon in an Leabharlann's yard, under orders to turn his horse for home if the keeper will not file them under Òrd an t-Seabhaig.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Hawk houses' registers

told_in.section: IV. Of the Hawk's Rolls

events.title: Mòrag's three lines to Òrd an t-Seabhaig
events.body: Mòrag nic Coinnich answers Òrd an t-Seabhaig in three lines in her own hand before dusk: the rolls will be filed under Òrd an t-Seabhaig in a press of their own, the houses may send a witness to see it, and a copy made in an Leabharlann's own hand goes back to them whenever they ask.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Hawk houses' registers

told_in.section: IV. Of the Hawk's Rolls

events.title: A paper filed under its sender's name
events.body: For the first time an Leabharlann files a paper under a name its sender sets against the name its own register gives; Mòrag nic Coinnich enters the fact plainly, and beneath it that she does not think an Leabharlann has any business teaching Òrd an t-Seabhaig what to call themselves.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Hawk houses' registers

told_in.section: IV. Of the Hawk's Rolls

events.title: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh's first foot-note
events.body: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh's first note of what the record could not learn concerns the northern shires: the census clerks were told the figures and did not count them, and the figures they were told were the Moot's.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tional nan Tuathach's figures given to the census clerks

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag's note sent north to Frayne

events.title: Beathag's note sent north to Frayne
events.body: A clerk of an Leabharlann sends Daniel Frayne a copy of Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh's first foot-note, naming the census clerks' reliance on Tional nan Tuathach's own figures; Frayne keeps it in his private book beside the day he gave them, judging her a chronicler the north may trust.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh's first foot-note

told_in.section: III. Of Tormod Pinn's Last Winter

events.title: The record-chests called in
events.body: Mòrag nic Coinnich's clerks go to thirty shire towns to bring their record-chests to Muileann chaol. At Seann Tarr the shire's keeper burns the chest sooner than send it, saying that the shire's record belongs in the shire. He is fined; the chest is lost.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mòrag nic Coinnich calls the shire chests in

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Seann Tarr keeper meets the clerks at the gate

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Seann Tarr keeper fined for the burning

events.title: Mòrag nic Coinnich calls the shire chests in
events.body: Mòrag nic Coinnich sends her own clerks along the roll to bring every shire's record-chest to Muileann chaol, judging a history kept in forty scattered chests no history at all but forty separate hopes of one day being read together.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The record-chests called in

told_in.section: V. Of the Chests Called In

events.title: The Seann Tarr keeper meets the clerks at the gate
events.body: The shire keeper who burned his own chest at Seann Tarr meets Mòrag's clerks at the gate the next morning, his coat still smelling of the smoke, and repeats to them plainly that the shire's record belongs in the shire.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The record-chests called in

told_in.section: V. Of the Chests Called In

events.title: Cathair naomh sends its rolls
events.body: The keeper of Cathair naomh in the north sends her shire's rolls to the library in two carts, with the town's own chronicle, kept by one family for four generations. Mòrag nic Coinnich enters it as the best-kept shire record received.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cathair naomh's chronicle carried south by its own keeper

events.title: Cathair naomh's chronicle carried south by its own keeper
events.body: The eldest daughter of the family that has kept Cathair naomh's town chronicle four generations rides the two carts south herself and unpacks them at Mòrag nic Coinnich's own table, Eachdraidh na Rìoghachd begun by her great-grandmother on the back of an unused rent-roll.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cathair naomh sends its rolls

told_in.section: V. Of the Chests Called In

events.title: A fourth coffer from Ros gheal
events.body: The Ros gheal carter comes south again the next spring with a fourth coffer of birth-rolls found in a shut room at the houses' oldest altar, and reports that the houses read Mòrag's three lines aloud in their hall and said nothing of them after, which in Oirthir an t-Seabhaig is how a thing is accepted.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Hawk houses' registers

told_in.section: IV. Of the Hawk's Rolls

events.title: The Seann Tarr keeper fined for the burning
events.body: The council fines the old keeper of Seann Tarr for burning the shire's chest; he pays without argument and without apology, and whatever the chest held of the shire's two centuries is lost entire.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The record-chests called in

told_in.section: V. Of the Chests Called In

events.title: The Seann Toll chest
events.body: Seann Toll in the north sends its chest willingly and asks for a copy of all that is in it. Mòrag nic Coinnich's clerks make the copy, and the shire's copy is the pattern for every copy the library has made since.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seann Toll's copy becomes the pattern

events.title: Seann Toll's copy becomes the pattern
events.body: The full transcription Mòrag's clerks make for Seann Toll, bound and set beside the original before either leaves the shire's hall, becomes the pattern every later shire's copy is cut to.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Seann Toll chest

told_in.section: V. Of the Chests Called In

events.title: The library enlarged
events.body: Leabharlann Muileann chaol doubles its holdings and takes several lesser archives of the provinces into one record. From this time the history of Dia-thìr is kept in one place and not in many.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The shires' chests counted

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Frayne puts the calling-in to Tional nan Tuathach's own room

events.title: Frayne puts the calling-in to Tional nan Tuathach's own room
events.body: Reading the notice of the calling-in, Daniel Frayne calls the room at Caol mhòr together and asks it plainly whether Tional nan Tuathach should offer its own books south now that the council has shown a wish to gather every shire's record.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The library enlarged

links.label: Follows from
links.title: No northern chest

told_in.section: V. Of the Chests Called In

events.title: No northern chest
events.body: No Tuathaich record is called in. The Moot's minute-books, the schools' registers, the churches' registers and the vigil-books of Baile chrom stay in the north, in private keeping, as they always have.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Frayne puts the calling-in to Tional nan Tuathach's own room

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tional nan Tuathach's minute declining to send its books

events.title: Tional nan Tuathach's minute declining to send its books
events.body: After an evening's debate, the room's minute at Caol mhòr records no vote by count and no reason beyond two words its clerk sets down at the close of the sitting: *kept north.* No cart of Tional nan Tuathach's own books goes south that year or after.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: No northern chest

told_in.section: V. Of the Chests Called In

events.title: The library's new wing
events.body: The enlarged library is housed in a new wing at Muileann chaol, built of the grey stone of the Sloc Mòr's spoil. The chests of the provinces fill three floors. The fourth is left empty for what was not sent.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The new wing's three floors and the empty fourth

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag's first foot-note on An t-Ùrlar Falamh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The tally of the calling-in read floor by floor

events.title: The new wing's three floors and the empty fourth
events.body: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh walks the new wing at Muileann chaol before its chests are carried up, and finds three floors built to hold the provinces' returns, town chronicles and vigil-books, and a fourth, raised to the same measure, left empty for a record that has not been sent.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The library's new wing

told_in.book: Of the Empty Floor and the Banked Fire
told_in.section: I. Of the Fourth Floor

events.title: Beathag's first foot-note on An t-Ùrlar Falamh
events.body: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh keeps Tormod Pinn's list at the front of the year's book unchanged and adds, beneath it, her own foot-note that the fourth floor stands ready and that no cart has come, judging the sentence plainer than any she could set beside it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The library's new wing

told_in.book: Of the Empty Floor and the Banked Fire
told_in.section: I. Of the Fourth Floor

events.title: The tally of the calling-in read floor by floor
events.body: Reading the whole tally of the calling-in set out floor by floor for the first time, Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh finds that every shire the council's roll accounted for sent something, willing or not, and that the one record never asked for is the one never received.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The library's new wing

told_in.book: Of the Empty Floor and the Banked Fire
told_in.section: I. Of the Fourth Floor

events.title: The branch line to Àth leathan closed
events.body: The Rail Board shuts the branch line to Àth leathan, pleading the falling yield of the western pits. The Tuathaich pits go on working, and their coal goes by cart to the western ports and by boat from there.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Àth leathan branch shut for falling yield

events.title: The Àth leathan branch shut for falling yield
events.body: Comhairle nam Mèinnean withdraws its overseers from Àth leathan along with the branch line, its own wages no longer answering for the western pits' falling yield, and the pits pass, without any charter forbidding it, into the keeping of the hewers who work them.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The branch line to Àth leathan closed

told_in.book: Of the Empty Floor and the Banked Fire
told_in.section: II. Of the Arrears at Àth leathan

events.title: The Moot's hewers take the pits
events.body: The Board's overseers are withdrawn from Àth leathan, and the Tuathaich hewers there go on working the pits under their own pit captains, paying the Crown's fifth under the Leòid ruling. The Board takes the payments and enters them as arrears.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Àth leathan hewers pay the fifth and are entered in arrears

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first Àth leathan coal carted to Seann Bhral

events.title: The Àth leathan hewers pay the fifth and are entered in arrears
events.body: The pit captains the Àth leathan hewers choose from their own number weigh every cart and set by An Crùn's fifth under Breith Leòid, sending word south each season; Comhairle nam Mèinnean takes the payments when a carrier brings them and enters them in its own books as arrears.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Moot's hewers take the pits

told_in.book: Of the Empty Floor and the Banked Fire
told_in.section: II. Of the Arrears at Àth leathan

events.title: The first Àth leathan coal carted to Seann Bhral
events.body: The pit captains at Àth leathan send the season's first coal south by cart rather than by rail, three days slower on the road but loaded and sent on the hewers' own choosing, down to the coal factors' yards at Seann Bhral in the west.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Moot's hewers take the pits

told_in.book: Of the Empty Floor and the Banked Fire
told_in.section: II. Of the Arrears at Àth leathan

events.title: Cnoc thais in the western hills
events.body: At Cnoc thais in the western hills the Tuathaich pits pass to their hewers when the Board's overseers leave, and the father of the pit captain Tom Varley is chosen to keep the accounts. Here the town's own register of the pits begins.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Sam Varley opens the pit's own book at Cnoc thais

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tom Varley runs the book's errands

events.title: Sam Varley opens the pit's own book at Cnoc thais
events.body: When Comhairle nam Mèinnean's overseer leaves Cnoc thais, Sam Varley, who has kept a private tally beside Comhairle nam Mèinnean's own scale for eleven years, opens a book of the pit's own accounts headed only with the day and the pit's name, the earliest page the town's register still keeps.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cnoc thais in the western hills

told_in.book: Of the Empty Floor and the Banked Fire
told_in.section: III. Of the Register at Cnoc thais

events.title: Tom Varley runs the book's errands
events.body: Sam Varley's small son Tom, not yet old enough for the pit, carries the figures the book wants between the scale-house and his father's table; told that a book kept honest for nobody outlasts one kept honest only for someone watching, he carries them straight all the same.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cnoc thais in the western hills

told_in.book: Of the Empty Floor and the Banked Fire
told_in.section: III. Of the Register at Cnoc thais

events.title: The Sligeanach's great year
events.body: An Sligeanach Fad' às, the roadside tavern by Ceann bhàn on the southern road, is sold to a family of drovers from Achadh mhòr, who build a second hall for the drove trade. It becomes the greatest house on the old mining roads.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A dubhan tank at An Sligeanach Fad' às

links.label: Leads to
links.title: An Sligeanach Fad' às sold to a family of drovers

events.title: An Sligeanach Fad' às sold to a family of drovers
events.body: The family that kept An Sligeanach Fad' às three generations sells it to drovers new to the trade, who raise a second hall beside the first; within a few years it is the largest house on the old mining roads, grown fat on the drove trade as the coal roads empty.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Sligeanach's great year

told_in.book: Of the Empty Floor and the Banked Fire
told_in.section: III. Of the Register at Cnoc thais

events.title: The eastern fishing grounds fail
events.body: For the second year together the herring do not come to the grounds off the mouth of the Abhainn chaol below Seann Dunn. The east-coast boats go north to fish the grounds off Caol mhòr, which the licence law keeps for them, and the Tuathaich boats are pushed farther out.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The herring fail a second year off Seann Dunn

events.title: The herring fail a second year off Seann Dunn
events.body: The herring do not return, a second season together, to the grounds off Seann Dunn, and the east-coast boats, finding their own waters empty, take to fishing the grounds off Caol mhòr that the licence law has long kept for the northern boats.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The eastern fishing grounds fail

told_in.book: Of the Empty Floor and the Banked Fire
told_in.section: IV. Of the Failing Grounds

events.title: Inis mhin's boats
events.body: Pushed from their grounds by the eastern boats, the Tuathaich boats of Inis mhin fish the deep water beyond the northern isles. Two are lost in the first year and none after, and the catch of Inis mhin passes that of Caol mhòr.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Inis mhin's boats pass Caol mhòr's own catch

events.title: Inis mhin's boats pass Caol mhòr's own catch
events.body: Pushed from their nearer grounds by the crowding of east-coast boats, the boats of Inis mhin take the deep water beyond the northern isles; two are lost the first year and none after, and before the next season is out the catch they bring in passes what Caol mhòr itself takes from the grounds the law still calls its own.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Inis mhin's boats

told_in.book: Of the Empty Floor and the Banked Fire
told_in.section: IV. Of the Failing Grounds

events.title: Raghnall mac Mhuirich, keeper
events.body: Mòrag nic Coinnich lays down the keepership after some thirty years. Raghnall mac Mhuirich, her deputy, becomes keeper of Leabharlann Muileann chaol.

links.label: Same person
links.title: The keeper's word at an Leabharlann

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mòrag nic Coinnich lays down the keepership

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall mac Mhuirich made keeper

events.title: Mòrag nic Coinnich lays down the keepership
events.body: Mòrag nic Coinnich, two-and-seventy and thirty years and more in the chair, lays down the keepership of an Leabharlann, walking the fourth floor once more with Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh and saying only that she built the room and leaves the asking to whoever holds the chair after her.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raghnall mac Mhuirich, keeper

events.title: Raghnall mac Mhuirich made keeper
events.body: Raghnall mac Mhuirich, fifty that year, takes the chair Mòrag nic Coinnich lays down and changes nothing of an Leabharlann's hours or custom in his first year, a steadiness the clerks under him come to value in a season when little else about the kingdom's coal holds steady.

events.title: The coal price at the fair
events.body: The Board cuts its sales, and the price of coal-fuel at the fair at Muileann òg doubles. The fair's court fixes a ceiling price and cannot hold it.

events.title: The fair's ceiling set on coal and broken in every stall
events.body: When Comhairle nam Mèinnean cuts its sales and the price of coal-fuel at Muileann òg doubles, the fair's court sets a ceiling price by its long custom; within a season no factor sells at it, the coal not reaching the stalls at the named price, and the wardens do not cry the ceiling's breaking.

events.title: Beathag's foot-note on the capital's cold
events.body: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh's foot-note for the year names what the record cannot learn: how many grates in the capital's poorer wards went unlit for want of coal, a count no census asked for and no shire kept, so that an Leabharlann holds no reckoning of its own kingdom's cold.

events.title: Coal thieves at Cnoc fhiadhaich
events.body: Households of Cnoc fhiadhaich are found picking coal from the spoil-heaps to burn, and the Board posts watchmen there. The watchmen are men of the town, and see nothing.

events.title: The watchmen at Cnoc fhiadhaich see nothing
events.body: Comhairle nam Mèinnean posts watchmen of the town itself over the spoil-heaps at Cnoc fhiadhaich against households picking coal to burn; every night of the posting the watchmen see nothing, though the heaps grow lower and the poorer grates burn warmer than the fair's price could otherwise buy.

events.title: The capital's poorer streets burn short hours
events.body: In the capital's poorer wards the street lamps burn shorter hours than the council's lighting order requires, the keepers no longer able to afford in full an order written for coal at half the price it now costs; the council's own notice calls the shortening a saving.
